Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

The Report is the tenth Environmental, Social and Governance ( 'ESG' ) Report of China Medical System Holdings Limited (the 'Company' , together with its subsidiaries, the 'Group' or 'CMS' ). This is an annual report, which covers the fiscal year from January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025 (the 'Reporting Period' ) with some additional related information incorporated that may have occurred outside the Reporting Period.

The Report is prepared as per Appendix C2 Environmental, Social and Governance Reporting Code of Main Board Listing Rules issued by the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited ( 'HKEX' ), with reference to the SGX Core ESG Metrics published by the Singapore Exchange ( 'SGX' ). Meanwhile, the Report refers to and responds to issues concerned by the United Nations 2030 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), MSCI-ESG rating, and S&P Corporate Sustainability Assessment (CSA), with the combination of the Company' s business development and ESG practices.

The Report discloses the Group' s risk management initiatives and operational performance in ESG domains conforming to the principles of 'Materiality' , 'Quantitative' , 'Balance' and 'Consistency' mentioned in the Environmental, Social and Governance Reporting Code . Unless otherwise indicated, the scope of the Report is the same as that of the 2025 Annual Report of the Group, and includes the Company, its wholly-owned subsidiaries and majority-owned subsidiaries.

The materials and cases disclosed in the Report were from the Group' s relevant reports and archives. The Group undertakes that the Report does not contain any false information, misleading statements, or material omissions, and is responsible for the content of the Report as to its authenticity, accuracy, and completeness.

The Report can be accessed and downloaded from HKEX' s website (www.hkexnews.hk), SGX' s website (www.sgxgroup.com), and the Group' s website (www.cms.net.cn). For further consultation, any opinion or suggestion regarding the Report, please contact the Group via ir@cms.net.cn.

Steady progress delivers lasting impact. CMS will continue to uphold its mission of 'providing competitive products and services to meet unmet healthcare needs' . Working in close partnership with our stakeholders, we will continue to move forward on the shared path of protecting human health and advancing planetary sustainability-together building a future that is healthier, more inclusive, and truly sustainable.

Time brings renewed brilliance. In 2025, the global landscape experienced profound adjustments, geopolitical realignments, accelerating technological revolutions, escalating climate risks, and rapid transformation amid multiple changes in regulation, payment, and innovation competition across the pharmaceutical industry. The United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development has also entered a critical phase of overcoming challenges and breaking through bottlenecks. Against this evolving backdrop, the Group takes 'high-quality sustainable development' as its core, and deeply embeds ESG principles into its corporate strategy and operations. Guided by a long-term perspective, the Group actively fulfills its responsibilities as a corporate citizen, maintains strategic resolve amid uncertainty, and demonstrates its commitments through concrete actions.

We advance to realize 'health for all' . Driven by the dual engines of 'product strength and commercialization,' we deepen the global collaborative R&D network and strengthen the in-house R&D system, continuously increasing R&D expenditure in advanced therapies, rare diseases, and areas of unmet medical need, promoting faster translation of innovative achievements into clinically accessible treatment practices. At the same time, upholding the principle of inclusive benefit, we actively promote equitable access to medical resources through initiatives such as reasonable pricing practices, drug assistance programs, and public health education. These efforts are designed to overcome geographic and economic barriers, strengthen healthcare delivery capacity in less-developed regions, and meaningfully fulfill our responsibilities in advancing public health. We also give back to society and jointly build resilient communities through public welfare actions, and promote social inclusion and common development through projects such as disaster relief, rural revitalization, care for vulnerable groups, and investment in education.

Guided by high standards of corporate governance, operational management, and business ethics, CMS embeds compliant operations and risk management and control into key processes including R&D, manufacturing, sales, human resources, finance, supply chain, and information security, improves forward-looking risk identification, early warning, and emergency response coordination mechanisms, strictly safeguards the bottom lines of integrity, anti-fraud, and data compliance, and continuously enhances transparency and accountability. We leverage digitalization and AI to drive process online enablement and lean management, improve operational efficiency and decision-making quality, and strengthen organizational resilience. We continue to strengthen our talent development framework and organizational support systems, strengthen competency and pipeline building for key positions, advance training empowerment and occupational health and safety management, and foster a workplace culture that inspires creativity, respects diversity, and cares for well-being, sharing development achievements with employees. At the same time, we have built a synergistic mechanism spanning the entire value chain, from innovation incubation to commercialization, while enforcing rigorous quality and safety controls at every stage and systematically managing environmental and social risks across our supply chain. In close partnership with industry stakeholders, we actively promote the development of a responsible, transparent, and resilient collaborative ecosystem, continuously creating shared value.

We deeply recognize that climate change has become a key issue for the shared future of humanity. The Group proactively addresses climate risks, strives to improve the efficiency of energy and resource use, strengthens carbon emissions and water-use management, and continuously upgrades our mechanisms for identifying, assessing, and managing climate-related risks. At the same time, we actively explore synergistic pathways for the integrated development of environmental protection and the healthcare industry, contributing to a sustainable future in which people and nature coexist in harmony.

Steady progress delivers lasting impact. CMS will continue to uphold its mission of 'providing competitive products and services to meet unmet healthcare needs' . We will accelerate innovation and industrial upgrading through the development of new quality productive forces, advance compliant growth under high-standard corporate governance, respond proactively to climate challenges through green transformation, and extend the warmth of health through inclusive and public welfare action. Working in close partnership with our stakeholders, we will continue to move forward on the shared path of protecting human health and advancing planetary sustainability-together building a future that is healthier, more inclusive, and truly sustainable.
Chairman Lam Kong Hong Kong, China

CMS (stock code: 0867.HK, 8A8.SG) is a platform company linking pharmaceutical innovation and commercialization with strong product lifecycle management capability, dedicated to providing competitive products and services to meet unmet healthcare needs.

The Group focuses on unmet clinical needs and drives innovation through a dual approach of 'collaborative R&D and inhouse R&D' . We build an innovative pipeline centered on first-in-class (FIC) and best-in-class (BIC) products, delivering more breakthrough disease solutions for patients. As of 16 March, 2026, the Group' s differentiated innovative pipeline has expanded to approximately 50 products, with a total of 7 innovative drugs and 2 orphan drugs approved for marketing in China to address unmet medical needs, of which 4 innovative drugs and 2 orphan drugs have been included in China' s National Reimbursement Drug List and achieved large-scale clinical application, thus enhancing the affordability and accessibility of the innovative products and safeguarding the lives and health of more patients.

Focusing on such fields of specialty diseases as Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic(CKM), central nervous system, gastroenterology, ophthalmology, and skin health business, the Group has adhered to responsible business operations with high ethical standards. It has built a differentiated product portfolio with academic value and high-quality standards. Through its influential academic platform and network, the Group provides professional products and services that empower the continuous translation of scientific research into clinical diagnosis and treatment practices. The Group is also actively advancing the 'industrial internationalization' strategy, leveraging Singapore as a hub for emerging markets to build an efficient, end-to-end value chain with strong 'R&D - manufacturing - commercialization' synergies. Following our secondary listing in Singapore, we have further strengthened strategic recognition and connectivity to resources in international market, enabling new avenues for high-quality, sustainable growth.

Upholding the vision of 'becoming an innovation-leading, trustworthy specialty pharma'， CMS helps to improve the quality of patients' lives with quality products and services. While embracing the concept of sustainable development, the Group continuously improves its internal governance, upholds the baseline of product responsibility, respects and inspires employee value, proactively engages in public welfare and environmental protection activities, and joins hands with stakeholders to promote the healthy, harmonious, and sustainable development of the enterprise, environment, and society.

section_title: Statement of the Board of Directors
text: As the highest leadership and decision-making body for ESG-related matters, the Board of Directors of the Company places great importance on sustainable development, continuously strengthens the ESG governance framework, and promotes the integration of its own operations, ESG strategy, and social and environmental harmony, with the objective of creating long-term sustainable value for stakeholders.

section_title: Statement of the Board of Directors
text: The Company has formed a three-tier ESG governance framework consisting of the Board of Directors, the ESG Committee and the ESG Working Group. The Board of Directors of the Company is the highestlevel supervisory body for ESG strategy, management and execution, and is responsible for overall supervision, direction and review. The ESG Committee is chaired by the executive director of the Company, who leads the ESG management work, and three independent non-executive directors are appointed as committee members, among which Ms. Luo Ying was appointed as a member of the ESG Committee on March 16, 2026. The organization-wide ESG Working Group is responsible for comprehensively promoting and implementing ESG-related work.

section_title: Statement of the Board of Directors
text: In active response to the SDGs, the Board of Directors of the Company has developed a comprehensive ESG strategy and targets in line with the Group' s business practices, vision, and mission, and has set phased targets in areas such as healthcare accessibility, innovation and R&D, business ethics, product quality, employee training and development, employee diversity, occupational health and safety, greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, use of resources, and solid waste. During the Reporting Period, the Board of Directors convened four ESG Committee meetings to oversee and review the latest progress in healthcare accessibility, business ethics, product quality, employee training and development, ESG targets, and corresponding work plans.

section_title: Statement of the Board of Directors
text: Meanwhile, the Group also values two-way communication with internal and external stakeholders and has established a systematic and regular communication mechanism. It continuously collects and analyzes the expectations and suggestions of stakeholders, and incorporates them into the decisionmaking process for strategic planning and operational optimization to enhance the adaptability and sustainability of business development.

section_title: Statement of the Board of Directors
text: During the Reporting Period, the Group systematically assessed the materiality and priority of ESG issues through questionnaires, expert consultations, and other methods. The Group conducts assessments and impact analyses of ESG risks for issues with double materiality and financial materiality. Based on factors such as the probability of risk occurrence and the magnitude of impact, it develops response strategies and considers incorporating relevant issues into the Group' s overall risk management framework. The Board of Directors of the Company recognizes the significance of climate change impacts, and reviews the analysis results on climate change risks and opportunities, as well as climaterelated financial disclosures. In addition, the Board members continually update their knowledge of the latest climate change policies and industry trends.

section_title: Structure and Process of ESG Governance
text: The Company has formed a three-tier ESG governance framework consisting of the Board of Directors, the ESG Committee and the ESG Working Group to systematically advance the decision-making, execution, and supervision of ESG strategy from top to bottom. The ESG Committee consists of four directors, with Ms. Chen Yanling, Executive Director, Chief Financial Officer, and Vice President of the Group, serving as Chair of the Committee, among which Ms. Luo Ying was appointed as a member of the ESG Committee on March 16, 2026. The ESG Working Group is composed of ESG representatives from various departments and is responsible for implementing and reporting on specific ESG initiatives. The scope of authority at each tier, reporting procedures, and other details are comprehensively disclosed in the CMS Environmental, Social and Governance Committee Terms of Reference , which has been published on the Group' s official website for all stakeholders' reference.

section_title: Linking ESG Indicators to Management Performance
text: To further integrate ESG governance with the incentive system, the Group has formally established the CMS Non-financial Key Performance Indicators and Management Remuneration Linkage Mechanism . The mechanism incorporates key ESG indicators such as business ethics, product quality and safety, and climate change into the performance evaluation system for executive directors, senior management, and relevant management personnel, explicitly linking ESG indicators to 10% of the yearend bonus. This initiative aims to extend ESG targets from the strategic level of the Board of Directors to the front line of business implementation, promoting the management to comprehensively fulfill sustainability responsibilities while pursuing business performance. By directly linking ESG performance to remuneration incentives, the Group not only strengthens the execution of ESG initiatives, but also helps achieve an organic balance between long-term sustainable value and short-term operational performance, providing an institutional safeguard for its high-quality and responsible development.

The identification of material issues is a crucial step in building a sustainable development management system for enterprises. It helps clarify critical areas of responsibility and promotes the deep integration of ESG practices with strategic development. During the Reporting Period, the Group systematically reviewed sustainability-related issues by considering industry attributes, business characteristics, and changes in internal and external environments, and conducted the materiality assessment from two dimensions: 'impact on CMS' s finance and operations' (financial materiality) and 'impact on the economy, society, and environment' (impact materiality).
· Combining the current situation and the background of CMS

Based on the current operational status and development background of the Group, the Group reviewed business operations, value chain, and geographical distribution, identified relevant laws, regulations, and industry standards, analyzed the impact of its business on stakeholders, and systematically clarified the foundational environment for its sustainable development.

Based on the requirements of sustainability-related disclosure standards and guidelines, capital market-related rating requirements, benchmarking analyses of peer disclosure practices, and taking into account the Group' s operational circumstances, a final list of 23 issues was established.

The double materiality assessment this year was conducted through multiple approaches, including questionnaire and expert evaluations. During the Reporting Period, the Group engaged with stakeholders such as internal management, customers, suppliers, government authorities, and industry associations to thoroughly gather evaluations on the materiality of various ESG issues from both internal and external perspectives. A comprehensive analysis was conducted incorporating opinions from internal and external ESG experts.

Impact materiality assessment: Comprehensively considering both positive and negative impacts, actual and potential impacts, the Group assessed whether its performance on ESG-related issues would have significant impacts on the environment, economy, and society from dimensions such as impact scale, impact scope, probability of occurrence, and irreparability.

Financial materiality assessment: Considering the short-, medium-, and long-term time cycle, the Group comprehensively assessed the probability of occurrence and the degree of financial impact. By integrating aspects such as business continuity and relational dependency, the Group thoroughly evaluated the impact of relevant issues on the Group' s business model, business operations, financial condition, and other financial indicators across different cycles.

text: Issues with financial materiality | Risks | Opportunities | Response strategies Healthcare accessibility | Unreasonable pricing, insufficient supply at the grassroots level, or slow implementation of innovative drugs may lead to increased patient burden, affecting social image. | Enhancing accessibility helps expand market coverage, increase public recognition, and explore emerging market opportunities. | The Company has established a governance and control system centered on the Board of Directors and enhances medical accessibility and affordability comprehensively through fair pricing, promoting the inclusion of products in the NRDL, multi-level supply chain building, acceleration of innovative drug launches, expansion of emerging markets, nonprofit science education initiatives and drug donation activities, and the supportive training of healthcare professionals. Intellectual property protection | Infringement or mismanagement of intellectual property rights may lead to legal disputes, asset loss, and impact R&D progress and competitive advantage. | Strengthening end- to-end lifecycle management helps protect innovation outcomes and unlocks the commercial value of R&D. | The Group has established a specialized management system, a comprehensive process control system, a regular prevention and control mechanism, specialized training, and diverse monitoring and reporting channels for systematic intellectual property protection and risk management. Industry development promotion | Failure to keep pace with clinical needs or guideline updates may lead to insufficient product recognition, affecting market promotion. | Deep participation in the development of guidelines and academic consensus helps enhance product credibility through authoritative validation and market competitiveness. | The Group has leveraged its role as a bridge within the pharmaceutical industry to support the inclusion of core products in authoritative domestic and international treatment guidelines and expert consensus. Innovative research and development | High R&D investment and long cycles may lead to unrecoverable costs if clinical trials fail or approvals are delayed, affecting long-term performance. | Continued investment in innovation and strategic focus on the fields of specialty and rare diseases helps enrich the product line and drive long- term growth. | Focusing on patient needs, the Group continuously increases investment through independent R&D, industrial investment, and strategic cooperation, establishes a end-to-end lifecycle R&D system, concentrates on advantageous areas, efficiently advances clinical development and commercialization, and simultaneously strengthens intellectual property protection. Product and service quality | Unstable material quality, production or storage lapses may lead to drug safety issues, resulting in recalls and reputational damage. | Establishing a full value chain quality system helps ensure drug safety and shapes a professional and reliable brand image. | The Group has established a comprehensive quality system covering the entire process of source control, production and operation, storage and transportation, traceability management, and complaint handling, ensuring the quality of products and services through internal and external audits, system optimization, personnel assessment, and closed-loop rectification. Leveraging dedicated policies, end-to-end review of promotional materials, regular training for all employees, multi-level monitoring and assessment, and a whistleblower protection system, the Group comprehensively manages related risks.

Adhering to the original aspiration, the Group remains dedicated to addressing unmet needs. It upholds on the mission of 'providing competitive products and services to meet unmet medical needs'， and is committed to offering patients with more and better treatment options.

Committed to the innovation development strategy and guided by patient needs, the Group continues to increase R&D investment in drugs for serious diseases, chronic diseases, and rare diseases, continuously optimizes its innovation system and enriches its pipeline portfolio.

With the specialty-focused innovation R&D platform, the Group rapidly introduces global new and good drugs into China and other Asia-Pacific markets through multiple approaches, including industrial investment, strategic cooperation and in-house R&D, etc. The Group also efficiently promotes clinical development and commercialization, improves the accessibility of cuttingedge global therapies, and provides better treatment options to patients, thereby realizing the clinical and social value of its products.
Innovative Pipeline Products Mainly FIC and BIC
Innovative Drugs Approved for Marketing in China
Innovative Drugs Approved for Marketing in China

During the Reporting Period, the Group had a turnover of RMB 9,385.6 million in the case that all medicines were directly sold by the Group, its total R&D expenditures (including both capitalised and expensed amounts) increased by 40.5% to RMB 1,058.4 million in 2025 compared to last year, and its total R&D expenditures as a percentage of turnover increased by 2.6 percentage points to 11.3% in 2025 comparing to last year. With the expansion of innovative products, the Group has developed a pipeline of approximately 50 short-, medium- and long-term innovative products with a relatively high level of innovation and differentiated clinical advantages. The Group' s R&D capabilities have earned recognition from third-party institutions. During the Reporting Period, the Group' s Shenzhen subsidiary was selected in '2025 Top 100 Chinese Pharmaceutical Enterprises in Chemical Drug R&D' by Yaozh.com.
During the Reporting Period, the Group added 5 quality innovative pipeline products:

In October, the Group obtained the exclusive rights to import, distribute, sell, and promote the nextgeneration anti-VEGF drug Brolucizumab Injection (BEOVU) for the treatment of diabetic macular edema (DME) in Mainland China. Leveraging its innovative advantages in ultra-small molecular and high concentration, it is anticipated to help more DME patients gain visual improvement and alleviate treatment burden.
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

In September, the Group obtained exclusive commercialization rights for two Class I innovative biologics, Silevimig Injection (passive immunization against rabies) and Vecantoxatug Injection (passive immunization against tetanus) in Mainland China and exclusive licensing rights for the rest of the Asia-Pacific region, the Middle East and North Africa. These products are expected to provide new preventive and therapeutic options of passive immunization for patients following tetanus and rabies exposure.

In January, the Group obtained the co-development rights (excluding AD) and exclusive commercialization rights in Mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan, and Singapore for the innovative long-acting anti-IL-4Rα humanized monoclonal antibody, Comekibart Injection (MG-K10), for the treatment of type 2 inflammatory diseases such as atopic dermatitis (AD), prurigo nodularis, asthma, and seasonal allergic rhinitis. The product enables a four-week dosing frequency, which is expected to improve patient adherence.

In January, the Group obtained exclusive right to develop, register, manufacture, import, export, and commercialize the improved new drug Benzgalantamine Gluconate Enteric-coated Tablets (ZUNVEYL) in Asia (excluding Japan and the Middle East region), Australia, and New Zealand. It is indicated for the treatment of mild to moderate dementia of the Alzheimer's type. It demonstrates a potentially better gastrointestinal safety profile to improve compliance of patients.

As of the last practicable date 3 , the Group already had 7 differentiated innovative drugs approved for marketing in China. Among which, ruxolitinib phosphate cream (vitiligo indication) was approved for marketing in China in January 2026, and Desidustat Tablets was approved for marketing in China in March 2026. In addition, 4 innovative drugs (VELPHORO, ILUMETRI, VALTOCO, and METOJECT) had been included in the NRDL, comprehensively enhancing drug accessibility and benefiting more patients in China.
3 The last practicable date was March 16, 2026.

text: CMS's Marketed Innovative Drugs The Group also made significant progress in multiple innovative pipeline products under development. As of the last practicable date, 6 innovative drugs were under review for the New Drug Application (NDA) in China , including Loberamisal for Injection (Y-3 for Injection), Silevimig Injection, Vecantoxatug Injection, Benzgalantamine Gluconate Enteric-coated Tablets (ZUNVEYL), Comekibart Injection (MGK10) for atopic dermatitis (AD) indication, and ruxolitinib phosphate cream for AD indication. Since 2025, the Group has newly granted 10 approvals for Investigational New Drug ( 'IND' ) in China, and has efficiently advanced the clinical development of multiple innovative products.
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

Meanwhile, leveraging its efficient R&D and management system for the full product lifecycle of innovative products, the Group continues to enhance its in-house R&D capabilities, focusing on new targets and cutting-edge technologies in advantageous specialty areas, including CKM, central nervous system, gastroenterology, ophthalmology, and skin health, with the aim of improving patients' quality of life. As of the last practicable date, the Group has steadily advanced about 6 in-house R&D projects with worldwide proprietary intellectual property into the clinical stage, including TYK2 Inhibitor CMS-D001 Tablets (intended for psoriasis, Atopic Dermatitis), GnRH Receptor Antagonist CMS-D002 Capsules (intended for uterine fibroids), GLP-1R/GCGR Dual Agonist CMS-D005 Injection (intended for obesity/overweight), Cardiac Myosin Inhibitor CMS-D003 Capsules (intended for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy), Complement Factor B Inhibitor CMS-D017 Capsules(intended for paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria and complement-mediated renal diseases) and a siRNA therapy targeting and inhibiting INHBE CMS-D008(intended for overweight/obesity). In addition, the Group' s in-house R&D pipeline also comprises more than 20 candidate products at the preclinical research stage.

As one of the major medical challenges posed to global human health, the improvement in treatment capabilities of rare diseases has attracted widespread attention. The Group pays close attention to the treatment needs of patients with rare diseases, providing this special group with better quality and more diversified treatment options. In January 2026, the Group' s self-developed innovative drug Complement Factor B Inhibitor CMS-D017 Capsules obtained IND approval in China. The product has demonstrated excellent efficacy and safety in preclinical studies and is being developed for clinical use in the treatment of a rare disease, paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria.
As of the end of the Reporting Period, 2 orphan drugs of the Group were approved for marketing in China:

Ursofalk (Ursodeoxycholic Acid Oral Suspension) was approved for marketing in China in July 2024 and was included in the Category B of NRDL in December 2025. Among its approved indications, one is a rare disease (for the treatment of liver disease associated with a condition called cystic fibrosis in children aged 1 month to 18 years), making it the first approved drug for this indication in China. Moreover, the product is an oral suspension that further meets clinical medication needs of patients with rare diseases and pediatric diseases due to its unique new variety, dosage form and specification as a pediatric drug, which is in line with the physiological characteristics of children.

The generic drug, Tetrabenazine Tablets, as a first-line drug for a rare disease named Huntington's disease, was approved for marketing in China in May 2023, and was included in the NRDL, which is expected to provide more accessible and affordable treatment options for patients with rare diseases.

Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

The Group actively joins various industry associations and participates in industry forums, academic seminars, and other academic exchange activities, engaging in academic interactions with experts and peers both domestically and internationally at all levels. It engages in discussions and shares practical experiences on the latest diagnostic and therapeutic technologies, as well as new drug development progress, in the fields of CKM, central nervous system, gastroenterology, ophthalmology, and skin health. Working together with industry participants, the Group coordinates efforts to support the highquality development of the healthcare industry in China and other developing countries.

To encourage the implementation of scientific research projects and the exploration of clinical applications, the Group actively responds to national initiatives and closely cooperates with renowned domestic universities, medical institutions, and charitable foundations in improving its scientific research system, cultivating scientific research talents, and accelerating the translation of medical innovation achievements, thereby promoting the sustainable development of clinical research in China across multiple dimensions. During the Reporting Period, the Group further deepened school-enterprise cooperation and strengthened the integrated interaction and convergence of industry, university, and research in the healthcare sector. The Group also made donations to the education foundations of several renowned universities to support discipline development, scientific research, talent cultivation, and the development of affiliated hospitals of medical schools.
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

The Board of Directors of the Company is the highest responsible body for matters related to improving healthcare accessibility. It is responsible for formulating relevant strategies and targets, and overseeing the implementation of the Company' s full value-chain medical programs, covering product R&D, service systems and capacity building, and the development of the industry ecosystem. The ESG Committee under the Board of Directors regularly reviews and continuously oversees the implementation of relevant strategies, policies, and works on an annual basis to ensure that initiatives are effectively implemented. The Group is committed to continuously improving the accessibility and affordability of pharmaceutical products through systematic management and practices, promoting the development of inclusive healthcare through concrete actions, and fulfilling the social responsibilities of a pharmaceutical company.

The Group has acknowledged resistance to antibiotics as one of the public health threats worldwide. To halt the global spread of antibiotic resistance and its impact on medical progress, the Group attaches great importance to the scientific and prudent use of antibiotic drugs, calls for enhanced management of relevant prescription drugs, and supports R&D and industry exchange addressing antibiotic resistance.

The Group firmly supports fair drug pricing mechanisms and attaches great importance to improving the affordability of pharmaceutical products in China and other developing-country markets. The major marketed products of the Group are supported by robust evidence-based medical evidence, enjoy a strong brand reputation, and offer relatively low daily treatment costs.

In the product pricing process, the Group strictly follows domestic laws, regulations, and regulatory policies related to drug prices, initiates pharmacoeconomic studies, and fully considers the actual costs and clinical value of drugs, and conducts fair pricing through standardized tendering procedures, to ensure the rationality and fairness of drug prices.

Meanwhile, the Group proactively promotes the inclusion of its innovative products in the NRDL through medical insurance negotiations to alleviate patients' financial burden and reduce pressure on medical insurance payments. As of the last practicable date, among the Group' s core marketed products, over 65% of them were included in the NRDL, and approximately 10% of them were included in the National Essential Drug List.
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

During the Reporting Period, 2 products of the Group, BEOVU (Brolucizumab Injection) and Ursofalk (Ursodeoxycholic Acid Oral Suspension), were newly included in the National Drug Catalogue for Basic Medical Insurance, Work-related Injury Insurance and Maternity Insurance (2025 Version) ( 'the 2025 NRDL' ). The Group' s marketed product, XinHuoSu (Recombinant Human Brain Natriuretic Peptide for Injection) has been included in the NRDL for consecutive years and was adjusted to the general list this time. Multiple innovative drugs (VELPHORO, ILUMETRI, and VALTOCO) successfully completed the NRDL renewal to consistently benefit patients.
The prices of the Group' s major marketed products can be found on the official websites of the National Healthcare Security Administration or drug procurement centers of different provinces.

The Group attaches great importance to the affordability of its products in developing country markets such as Southeast Asia and the Middle East. It complies with local government pricing policies and fully takes into account the level of economic and industry development across different countries and different regions within a country. It conducts comprehensive assessments of the following factors to formulate fair pricing strategies suited to local conditions: local economic growth rate, per capita disposable income level, healthcare system quality, product production and supply conditions, medical insurance affordability, and competitor pricing. Meanwhile, the Group actively participates in local government tenders, striving to reduce the economic burden of medication for patients in developing countries and contributing to the development of local medical and health security systems.
Improving Drug Accessibility in Emerging Markets

The Group collaborates with global pharmaceutical innovation partners, striving to bring high-quality and affordable pharmaceutical products to more patients in China and other developing countries, thereby contributing to improving healthcare standards in countries/regions primarily in Asia-Pacific emerging markets. The Group supports the Doha Declaration on TRIPS Agreement and Public Health , recognizing its significance in helping underdeveloped countries in need to gain access to medicines under certain circumstances. The Group recognizes and supports reasonable generic competition and makes its best efforts to improve healthcare accessibility across different geographies, especially in underdeveloped countries, contributing to the sustainable development of global healthcare.

The Group has been deeply engaged in the China market, continuously enriching the product pipeline layout and expanding indication coverage in therapeutic areas including CKM, central nervous system, gastroenterology, ophthalmology, and skin health, to meet the needs of various disease patients in China for safe, effective, and affordable medicines.
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

The Group has established a synergistic and complementary channels across public hospitals, nonpublic healthcare institutions, dual-channel pharmacies, chain drugstores, and e-commerce networks, thereby building a multi-tiered pharmaceutical supply system. Meanwhile, the Group is committed to eliminating health disparities for residents in underdeveloped regions, and actively promotes the expansion and penetration of the county-level and lower-tier markets, as well as economically backward areas, to provide communities with high-quality products at affordable prices. As of the end of the Reporting Period, the Group's marketed products have achieved extensive coverage in hospitals/ medical institutions/drugstores in China, significantly improving the accessibility of the products.

In order to improve the efficiency of the pharmaceutical supply, the Group supplies the pharmaceutical products to the local distributors, and provides reasonable packaging planning in advance for the delivery and transportation of pharmaceutical products. The Group also offers suggestions on the optimal transportation solutions to maximize the efficiency of the supply chain, so as to ensure the timeliness of pharmaceutical supply. The Group is also committed to using digital tools to address pharmaceutical supply issues in remote areas and community healthcare institutions. Leveraging its experience in building and applying digital management systems, it has provided long-term public welfare assistance to Nenang Ecological and Cultural Conservation Center in Doilungdeqen District, Lhasa, Tibet, and led the establishment of a fully digitalized and visual inventory management system for pharmaceutical supplies in the Center' s clinic, improving pharmaceutical supply efficiency, significantly shortening emergency response time, and enhancing the accessibility of medicines across geographic and time dimensions.
In addition, the Group is dedicated to shortening the time lag for Chinese patients to access innovative drugs, thereby accelerating the availability of innovative therapies to benefit more patients.

The innovative drug ruxolitinib phosphate cream (vitiligo indication) successively commenced pilot use under China's policy for the importation of clinically urgent medicines at designated medical institutions in the Hainan Boao Lecheng International Medical Tourism Pilot Zone, the Guangdong Province (Greater Bay Area), and the Beijing and Tianjin Free Trade Zones. As of the end of the Reporting Period, Boao Super Hospital has prescribed the product to near 7,500 patients with nonsegmental vitiligo, and a total of approximately 25 hospitals in Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Dongguan, Foshan, Zhongshan, Zhuhai, Jiangmen, Huizhou, Beijing, and Tianjin have provided prescription services for the product, reducing the time gap for Chinese vitiligo patients to access innovative drugs. Moreover, the localization technology transfer of the product is being orderly advanced, which may further improve the accessibility and affordability of global quality innovative drugs in China.
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

The innovative oral JAK1 inhibitor, povorcitinib, was included in the list of Breakthrough Therapeutic Drugs by the Center for Drug Evaluation of the NMPA in December 2025. This certification has the potential to accelerate the development and review process of the product in China, enabling patients with vitiligo in China to benefit from globally innovative therapies at an earlier date.

The improved new drug ZUNVEYL is the second oral therapy approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease in more than a decade. Leveraging its efficient allocation of resources and robust capabilities in registration promotion, the Group submitted the NDA in China for the product in July 2025, around six months after obtaining the rights of the product, enabling Chinese patients to benefit from an innovative Alzheimer's therapy with a potentially better gastrointestinal safety profile at an earlier date.

The Group is advancing its 'industrial internationalization' development strategy by extending the high-quality pipeline and mature commercialization capabilities accumulated in the China market to other developing country markets such as Southeast Asia and the Middle East. With a focus on addressing unmet local clinical needs, the Group leverages the established R&D system 'CMS R&D' , manufacturing system 'PharmaGend' , and commercialization system 'Rxilient' in a coordinated manner to comprehensively drive the full ecosystem development integrated R&D, manufacturing, and commercialization of the pharmaceutical industry in emerging markets, and enhance the accessibility of healthcare products and services locally.

Headquartered in Singapore as the Group' s base for its Asia-Pacific emerging market business, Rxilient has established subsidiaries or offices in Hong Kong, Taiwan Region, Malaysia, Vietnam, the Philippines, Indonesia, Thailand, and the United Arab Emirates. It employs local talents to run the business, providing employment opportunities and positions for local people.

Leveraging its rich industry resources, the Group supports Rxilient to reach collaborations with global pharmaceutical enterprises or biotech companies in developing markets such as Southeast Asia and the Middle East. During the Reporting Period, Rxilient continued to enrich its differentiated innovative product pipeline:

Obtained exclusive right to develop, register, manufacture, import, export, and commercialize the improved new drug, ZUNVEYL (for Alzheimer's disease), in Asia (excluding Mainland China, Japan, and the Middle East region);

Obtained the exclusive licensing rights for the Class I innovative biologics, Silevimig Injection (for passive immunization against rabies) and Vecantoxatug Injection (for passive immunization against tetanus), in the rest of the Asia-Pacific region outside Mainland China, the Middle East and North Africa;

Obtained exclusive licensing rights for Class 1 innovative drug, Y-3 for Injection (for acute ischemic stroke), in Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan, Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, in the Middle East and North Africa;
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

Obtained the co-development rights (excluding AD) and exclusive commercialization rights in Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan, and Singapore for the Class 1 innovative drug, MG-K10 (for atopic dermatitis, asthma, and seasonal allergic rhinitis).

Rxilient also actively promotes the registration, and commercialization of high-quality pharmaceutical products. As of the end of the Reporting Period, it had cumulatively submitted nearly 20 registration applications for pharmaceutical products and medical devices in the Asia-Pacific and the Middle East regions, establishing a diversified product portfolio covering CKM, central nervous system, autoimmune, ophthalmology, dermatology, and oncology. Among these, core innovative pipeline products have progressively achieved positive progress:
Ruxolitinib phosphate cream for vitiligo has officially launched sales in Hong Kong and Macau, and registration applications have been submitted in Singapore and Taiwan region;

Sucroferric Oxyhydroxide Chewable Tablets has been approved for marketing in Hong Kong and Macau and included under the category of 'Special Drug' on the Hong Kong Hospital Authority Drug Formulary, and the registration application has been submitted in Taiwan region;
Tildrakizumab Injection has been approved for marketing in Hong Kong, and the registration application has been submitted in Taiwan region;
The registration applications for ZUNVEYL have been submitted in Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, and the Macau and Taiwan regions;
The registration applications for Diazepam Nasal Spray have been submitted in Hong Kong and Taiwan regions, and it was approved for marketing in Singapore in January 2026.

Moreover, Rxilient accelerated the progress of the NPP (Named Patient Program) for innovative drugs in urgent clinical need in certain countries in Southeast Asia, allowing relevant patients to get drug therapies earlier before the product is formally approved for marketing to shorten the waiting time for Southeast Asian patients to use international quality innovative drugs. As of the end of the Reporting Period, the NPP for ruxolitinib phosphate cream for vitiligo has been implemented in Singapore and Malaysia.

The Group also promotes the re-education of local healthcare professionals in Southeast Asia. By organizing or participating in interactive exchanges and academic events for healthcare professionals, it facilitates discussions on cutting-edge medical technologies and outstanding clinical practices, empowering the competence building of local healthcare professionals. During the Reporting Period, Rxilient attended the 2025 European Society for Medical Oncology Asia Congress (ESMO Asia 2025), sharing with local oncology practitioners in the Philippines its experience in the treatment and management of recurrent metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (RM-NPC) using an innovative antiPD-1 immunotherapy. Through mentor-led re-education, it enhanced the oncology diagnostic and treatment capabilities of local healthcare professionals.
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

In addition, PharmaGend, an associate company of the Group based in Singapore, has gradually developed into an international one-stop pharmaceutical CDMO platform with high-standard drug manufacturing capabilities, empowering global pharmaceutical companies to rapidly enter emerging markets. As of the end of the Reporting Period, PharmaGend has established a manufacturing site of 30,000 square meters, has obtained a drug manufacturing license issued by the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) of Singapore, and has received multiple international certifications, including GMP （Good Manufacturing Practice) from HSA, Current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) certification from the U.S. FDA, and the audits by Swiss Qualified Person (QP). The annual capacity of its oral solid dosage (OSD) has reached 1.5 billion units, while capacity expansion for the construction of new production lines for nasal sprays, creams, and injectables, as well as a packaging center, is progressing smoothly. These efforts are expected to improve local drug manufacturing and supply capabilities and, to some extent, contribute to the advancement of the regional pharmaceutical industrialization level. Meanwhile, Rxilient and PharmaGend have actively collaborated to jointly advance the localization technology transfer of key products, with a view to achieving localized production as soon as possible and improving access to Global high-quality products in emerging markets. In addition, Rxilient also allows local distributors to supply products directly to the Southeast Asian market, enhancing the timeliness of drug distribution in developing countries and benefiting more patients.

By actively cooperating with industry associations and public welfare foundations in the relevant disease fields, and through diversified initiatives including patient caring programs, knowledge promotion events, drug donations and charity clinics, the Group enhances the popularization and publicity of disease and health knowledge, and raises public health awareness.

The Group initiated a disease knowledge popularization section 'CMS Sees' on its WeChat official account to further promote the popularization of disease knowledge. During the Reporting Period, the Group published a number of articles on its WeChat official account to disseminate the knowledge of kidney diseases, glaucoma, vitiligo, epilepsy, and psoriasis to the public in an easy-to-understand format.
Epilepsy public welfare and drug donation programs

To standardize emergency treatment for epilepsy and improve patients' ability to provide out-ofhospital emergency for epilepsy, the Group has assisted China Association Against Epilepsy (CAAE) in advancing diverse caring programs for epilepsy patients for two consecutive years, covering a wide geographic area. Moreover, the Group also supports several public welfare organizations in carrying out various epilepsy public education activities. These activities primarily comprise offline initiatives such as science popularization lectures, mutual assistance and communication between doctors and patients, and distribution of educational handbooks. They are also disseminated online through channels such as wechat articles, comics, and animated videos, thereby delivering scientific and easy-to-understand epilepsy emergency knowledge to a broad range of epilepsy patients and their families, primary-level medical staffs, and the general public through multiple dimensions and channels.
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

Additionally, the Group has partnered with foundation to implement the 'Escort With Love' drug donation program, aimed at alleviating the long-term treatment costs for patients experiencing recurrent and frequent seizures, improving drug accessibility, fulfilling the social responsibility of a pharmaceutical company, and contributing to enhancing the quality of life for epilepsy patients in China.
Rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis drug donation and popularization programs

For two consecutive years, the Group donated its products to patients with autoimmune diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis, for free via foundation to help them receive continuous and standardized treatment, relieve their financial burden, and improve their life quality and drug accessibility. At the same time, the Group also participated in the 'Journeying Together, Caring Along the Way' program, as well as the 'China Rheumatoid Arthritis Public Welfare Campaign' to offer authoritative disease education, rehabilitation guidance, and psychological support, while raising public awareness of autoimmune disease patients, combating social stigma, and helping patients regain confidence in their daily lives.
Public lectures on inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and drug donation programs

The Group has supported the large-scale public lectures named Salofalk 'World IBD Day (19 May)' for ten consecutive years, to raise IBD patients' cognition about the disease through consistent disease knowledge popularization. During the Reporting Period, the lecture' s online livestream received over 1.79 million views, effectively raising public awareness of IBD. The Group also actively initiated the dedicated charity initiative, the 'Healthy China - Medical Academic Exchange and IBD Patient Caring Program' , to help more IBD patients improve their quality of life and develop healthy lifestyle habits in diet, exercise, and emotional management. Additionally, the Group launched the 'Care for IBD Patients Program' , through which drugs were donated to IBD patients via a public welfare foundation, effectively reducing their financial burden and improving both the accessibility and continuity of standardized treatment.

The Group joined hands with the foundation to organize the public popularization program, 'AI-Powered Nephrology Education, Safeguarding Kidney Health' . By combining offline popularization and Q&A sessions led by doctors with an online AI-powered intelligent Q&A platform, the program promoted doctors' education for patients' disease management, enhanced chronic kidney disease patients' ognition of hyperphosphatemia, strengthened patients' attention to achieving blood phosphorus level targets, and improved awareness of phosphorus control.

The Group, in collaboration with multiple authoritative hospitals and DXY.cn, successfully held a series of public lectures on vitiligo themed 'Beautiful Confession - Public Lecture on Vitiligo' , helping patients enhance their cognition of vitiligo, learn about cutting-edge innovative therapies, and establish the concept of long-term disease management. All lecture livestreams were well organized and made available in DXY.cn' s 'Patient Education' section, forming a structured public education resource library for patients to review.

CMS remains committed to the principle of 'Compliance First', carries out responsible business operations with high business ethics standards, constantly improves internal governance and operational efficiency, and is devoted to providing stakeholders with high-quality and professional products and services.

section_title: Adhering to High Ethical Standards in Business Operations
Adhering to High Ethical Standards in Business Operations
text: The Group attaches great importance to risk management and internal controls and has established a risk management structure with clear roles and responsibilities. The Board of Directors is the highest decision-making body for the Company' s comprehensive risk management. Each year, the Group reports the annual audit work plan, audit findings, risk warnings, improvement measures, and progress updates to the Company' s Board of Directors. The Audit Committee under the Company' s Board of Directors is responsible for reviewing the work plans and results of internal and external audits, in order to ensure sufficient assistance to the Board in supervising and reviewing the effectiveness of the Group' s risk management and internal control system and to timely identify significant risks that may affect the Group' s operations.

section_title: Adhering to High Ethical Standards in Business Operations
text: The Group has established the Management Committee composed of executive directors and senior management. The Committee reviews the identification of significant risks and determines the response priorities, as well as oversees the implementation of the Group' s risk management. During the Reporting Period, through monthly Management Committee meetings, it systematically reviewed the status of compliance and risk management, focusing on developing response measures for potential risk issues in business operations. Meanwhile, the Compliance Department of the Group regularly shared industry compliance developments and reported the potential risks regarding compliance management and the progress of internal control directly to the executive directors and senior management, to further strengthen the prevention and control of internal systemic risks.

section_title: Adhering to High Ethical Standards in Business Operations
text: The Group continues to consolidate the 'three lines of defense' risk management and control system, clearly defining responsibilities at all levels to effectively carry out risk identification, assessment, response, and supervision, thereby consolidating the foundation of internal risk management.

section_title: Adhering to High Ethical Standards in Business Operations
text: The Group continuously optimizes its risk management system, policies, and work procedures to comprehensively identify and control potential risks. According to internal actual needs, internal audit work is carried out, and the Group' s audit plan covers all operating entities and major business segments at least annually. During the Reporting Period, the Group conducted 11 internal audits, covering areas such as expenses, procurement, and compliance risk inspections. During the audit process, the Group applied data analysis to identify potential risks at key control points and propose optimization suggestions. All audit results are based on the CMS Internal Audit Policy , forming special reports submitted for management review. The corrective actions and rectification progress of the audited units are dynamically tracked, creating an 'audit-feedback-improvement' closed-loop management process to continuously enhance the level of risk prevention and control.

section_title: Adhering to High Ethical Standards in Business Operations
text: During the Reporting Period, based on internal risk identification and management, the Group also emphasized the control of risks related to sustainable development. The Group has initially conducted assessments and impact analyses of the risks and opportunities associated with material ESG issues and is considering gradually integrating relevant ESG risks into the Company' s overall risk management system to enhance the ability to respond to ESG risks.

text: Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

CMS consistently places compliant operations and business ethics at the core of corporate development, considering them as the cornerstone of sustainable growth. The Group strictly complies with the laws and regulations of the People' s Republic of China and other countries and regions where it operates and invests. The Group focuses on establishing a scientific and systematic risk identification and control system to comprehensively monitor, prevent, and manage compliance and business ethicsrelated risks that may arise in different operational segments. This provides a solid guarantee for the Group' s long-term stable and healthy development.

Anti-corruption management is a core component of the Group' s compliance management system. The Group has established and implemented internal regulations to build a cross-departmental anticorruption supervision system, supplemented by systematic control systems and employee training mechanisms, to comprehensively strengthen the Group's anti-corruption risk defense through closedloop management.

The Group has established the CMS Anti-Fraud Management Policy, CMS Internal Audit Policy, CMS Compliance Management Policy , and other standards and regulations, which explicitly require all employees to refrain from engaging in any improper practices, such as bribery, corruption, fraud, extortion, money laundering, paying or accepting any form of facilitation fees within the Group or during interactions with stakeholders, including affiliated companies, media, governments, distributors, suppliers, and healthcare professionals. Moreover, the Group explicitly prohibits employees from intentionally engaging in fraudulent or illegal activities to gain undue personal benefits at the expense of the Group' s economic interests, or to seek undue economic benefits for the Group that may also result in undue personal benefits.

The Group evaluates and analyzes the latest laws, regulations and regulatory trends at least once a year, and assesses, reviews, and updates the internal policies and procedures related to anti-corruption and compliance management based on the review of historical work and risk control results. The relevant policies and regulations can only be issued and applied after the interdepartmental modification and review and the approval and sign-off by the executive directors. During the Reporting Period, the Group comprehensively reviewed and supplemented internal policy documents by benchmarking them against relevant laws, regulations as well as executive regulations that were newly issued in the year. The Group revised various internal compliance standard operating procedures, continuously strengthening compliance and business ethics management.

The Group has established a training mechanism on business ethics and anti-corruption, which covers all full-time, part-time, intern and labor dispatch employees (including the Board members, the management and general employees). The Group places significant emphasis on business ethics and anti-corruption training for the Board members, and continuously enhances their awareness of compliance and capabilities to perform their duties. Additionally, the Group also supports Board members to participate in various training programs organized by professional institutions. During the Reporting Period, all members of the Company's Board of Directors have received training on anti-corruption and business ethics, which covered regulatory requirements for the industry, industry updates, the Group' s compliance system and management strategy, directors' responsibilities, etc.
The Group also actively provides training and publicity related to anti-corruption and business ethics to all employees and has established a comprehensive training system.
▎ Executive directors and mid-level and senior management

During the monthly meetings of the Management Committee, the Group's Compliance Department provides training on anti-corruption and business ethics to the executive directors and mid-level and senior management team, and conveys the latest compliance requirements of the industry and the regulatory authorities.
Based on the CMS Academy, the Group offers online video training courses for all employees, including business ethics training, system revision/policy updates, or system control function launches.
Since 2019, the Group has organized education and training on policies related to anti-corruption and business ethics for all employees for seven consecutive years.
The new employee onboarding training covers anti-corruption-related content

The Group incorporates compliance knowledge examinations into the training of marketing and sales promotion staff, and links the examination results to team performance evaluations to strengthen employees' emphasis on compliance.

While systematically conducting business ethics training, the Group continuously deepens the promotion of a compliance culture. The Group regularly disseminates policy interpretations and compliance updates to all employees on a monthly basis, while simultaneously updating the 'I want to ask a compliance question' online section. Through monthly meetings of the regional compliance team, the Group focuses on communicating compliance matters and providing targeted responses to feedback from the business frontline. In addition, the Group utilizes AI technology to embed a compliance knowledge base within the internal digital platform, supporting employees with instant access to guidance through various training resources such as videos and documents. Additionally, it features an intelligent Q&A function, facilitating all employees in querying and learning compliance knowledge, thereby building a compliance culture ecosystem characterized by full participation, endto-end coverage, and real-time response.

During the Reporting Period, the Group organized training on anti-corruption and business ethics 1 time, covering compliance policy interpretation, work regulations, and compliance Q&As and guidance, to embed compliance principles. The Group also conducted integrity and self-discipline training for all employees, continuously fostering an atmosphere of integrity and efficiency within the organization.

The Group has established a business ethics and anti-corruption monitoring system that covers all aspects of business operations. The Company' s Board of Directors is responsible for overseeing the effectiveness of the compliance risk control procedures, as well as directing, supervising and approving the relevant work on anti-corruption and business ethics of the Group. During the Reporting Period, the Board of Directors has reviewed and evaluated the internal and external audit results, improvement measures, and progress related to business ethics and anti-corruption.
The Group has a well-established cross-departmental coordination system to comprehensively monitor and prevent anti-corruption risks, ensuring the effective implementation of all policies.

The Compliance Department is primarily responsible for maintaining and improving the Group's control systems, regulations, standards and working framework related to anti-unfair competition, anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and business ethics, monitoring the daily implementation and conducting closed-loop management, and performing effective review and oversight of compliance risks;
The Legal Department is responsible for controlling the legal risks of each stage of the Group's operations;

The Finance and Accounting Center has developed financial management measures within the compliance framework to oversee the entire process from expense budgeting, reimbursement to expenditure, and in the meantime, leveraged the digital management system to strengthen the review and process control, enhancing the transparency of expenses and ensuring compliance of income and expenditure across all internal operation segments;

As a keyline of defense for the Company's risk management, the Audit Department has established a risk management-oriented audit system, covering finance, internal controls, operations management, information system, and fraud investigation across the Group;

The Audit Department conducts internal audits for all operating entities of the Group at least once a year, to identify and manage the compliance risks in operations. During the Reporting Period, the Audit Department conducted business ethics and anti-corruption audits for the Group and its subsidiaries, to identify and assess the risks in all business processes including operation, procurement, promotion, marketing, investment, etc., and continuously tracked the implementation of improvement measures.

Internal Audits Related to Business Ethics and Anti-corruption The Group' s Audit Department is responsible for the internal audit work of the Group and its subsidiaries, including audits on business ethics and anti-corruption. When issues involve corruption, fraud, and other violations of business ethics, the Group will conduct investigations and handle them in accordance with the CMS Anti-Fraud Management Policy . Additionally, during the Reporting Period, the Group underwent regular annual compliance special audits conducted by international partners. Based on the internal and external audit results, the Group has continuously refined its internal audit plans and procedures, and further enhanced the Group' s compliance management system to ensure the operational process strictly adheres to the code of business ethics.

During the Reporting Period, no significant risks related to business ethics and anti-corruption were identified in the internal or external audits aforementioned. The Group did not report any concluded legal cases related to corruption. In terms of prevention of bribery, extortion, fraud, and money laundering, and against unfair competition, the Group also did not violate any relevant laws and regulations that would have a significant impact on the Group' s business operations.

If an employee is suspected of improper conduct in business activities, such as corruption, bribery, etc., following investigation and confirmation, the Group will issue a warning to the employee and impose appropriate disciplinary action according to the severity of the conduct. The punishment may impact the employee' s promotion, and in severe cases, the employment relationship may be terminated. If the conduct constitutes a crime, the employee will be referred to the judicial authorities for criminal liability in accordance with the law. The Group has organized the study and signing of the CMS Integrity and Self-discipline Commitment by all employees for six consecutive years to reinforce their awareness of improper commercial conduct and enhance vigilance against such behavior. During the Reporting Period, the signing rate of the CMS Integrity and Self-discipline Commitment was 100%.
Abstract of the CMS Integrity and Self-discipline Commitment
Strictly abiding by the provisions related to integrity and self-discipline
Properly exercising authority and not using it to gain undue benefits for oneself or any specific related person
Not embezzling or occupying the resources of the Group, or leveraging own authority to influence or interfere with the Group's business
Resolutely resisting commercial bribery, not accepting any bribes from any supervisory entities or suppliers
Not offering bribes or soliciting bribes from any business-related personnel

The Group has established a systematic, end-to-end responsible marketing management mechanism, using specialized policies and operational guidelines as the institutional foundation, combined with regular training and case education to enhance compliance awareness among all employees. Through the integration of routine monitoring and quantitative assessments into business processes, the Group ensures that marketing activities are legal, compliant, truthful, and transparent. At the same time, the Group has established and facilitated internal and external feedback channels to promptly respond to and verify relevant complaints, forming a dynamic closed-loop management cycle of 'systemexecution-oversight-feedback' to maintain the Group's reputation and public trust.

On the basis of strictly abiding by the laws related to compliant promotion in each place of business operation, the Group has implemented policies such as the CMS Compliance Management Policy, the CMS Responsible Marketing Policy , etc., which are applicable to all employees (including the Board members, the management, and general employees) of the Group and its subsidiaries, such as the fulltime and part-time employees, interns, as well as contractors. During the Reporting Period, the Group introduced new marketing promotion standards for subsidiaries. The documents explicitly prohibit any marketing and promotion with exaggerated, deceptive, false and misleading content or using commercial bribery or other illegal means.

The Group is committed to presenting product efficacy in an objective, accurate, and truthful manner, and requires that all promotional activities and related materials be subject to internal compliance review to ensure consistency with applicable laws and regulations and the approval information issued by the national drug regulatory authority. Approved materials are uniformly coded, archived and incorporated into a dedicated resource library for centralized management. The Group also requires that all advertisements and promotions of prescription drugs are subject to application for advertisement approval from relevant government departments, which can only be published in the professional publications jointly designated by the Ministry of Health and the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) after approval is granted.

The Group has deeply integrated the concept of responsible marketing into the development of organizational capabilities, establishing a systematic and regular training system to ensure that all employees fully understand the compliance requirements in academic promotion, marketing, and advertising and adhere to relevant laws, regulations, and ethical standards, striving to strengthen a culture of responsible marketing.
Coverage of Responsible Marketing Related Training for Promotion Business Employees

During the Reporting Period, the Group conducted responsible marketing-related education and training activities through various forms such as regular training, specialized development, daily support, and process control:

Organizing monthly induction training and a quiz for new employees in marketing and promotion roles, with quiz participation and pass rates linked to the annual performance of the regional compliance team;
Holding monthly communication meetings with the promotion team, presenting and elaborating the latest responsible marketing control requirements and their implementation status;
Providing training on all products to all employees in marketing and promotion roles, to ensure that employees convey compliant and accurate product information during marketing activities;

Publishing and interpreting the latest industry compliance policies on the internal digital communication platform on a monthly basis, to facilitate the management and employees to learn about the updates of responsible marketing;

Timely providing on-line training to all employees in case of updates on internal responsible marketing regulations or policies, and requiring all employees in marketing and promotion business to participate in the training and pass the relevant test;

Creating the 'I want to ask a compliance question' section to provide a convenient and timely channel for employees to ask questions about responsible marketing; the Compliance Department will respond within one week upon receipt of the relevant enquiries;

Uploading on-line training courses and videos related to responsible marketing to the internal employee training platform, and opening the intelligent Q&A platform, to provide employees with a convenient channel to gain responsible marketing knowledge and acquire real-time answers to relevant questions.

The Group has established a multi-level, cross-departmental coordinated system for responsible marketing monitoring and assessment, forming a responsible marketing management framework from strategic planning, process control to post-audit.

The Group' s Operation Management Center carries out control and early warning of operation objectives, product strategies and business progress of each operation responsibility center of the Group. The Compliance Department supervises the entire process of marketing activities. In terms of expense control, the Group has established a strict system for application, payment, and reimbursement, with the Compliance Department, Finance and Accounting Department, and Legal Department jointly reviewing contracts, invoices, and on-site materials.

After the completion of the marketing and promotion activities, the Compliance Department of the Group generates the monthly analysis, review and assessment report based on the monthly routine monitoring, targeted spot checks and compliance KPI assessments. These reports are then submitted to the management based on the importance of the issues or risk levels. Each year, the Audit Department audits the compliance, authenticity and integrity of marketing and promotion expenses of all operation responsibility centers and subsidiaries in marketing and promotion business. In addition, the Group engages an independent third-party organization annually to conduct special audits to ensure the Group continues to operate with high standards of compliance requirements.

Building on its oversight governance structure, the Group has established a comprehensive responsible marketing monitoring and assessment process covering the entire 'pre-event, in-event, and post-event' workflow. Through a combination of internal and external approaches, the Group ensures continuous compliance in operations:
Developing IT system functionalities for compliance policy revision points and anomaly detection;
Conducting due diligence on medical institutions and suppliers.
Participating in due diligence on participating partners;
Regularly holding compliance communication meetings with partners.

During the Reporting Period, no significant risks related to responsible marketing practices were identified within the Group according to the related unannounced inspections and audits. The Group was not subject to any lawsuits alleging excessive promotion, misleading claims, or consumer deception.

In addition, the Group conducts monthly assessments of compliance and responsible marketing for employees engaged in marketing and promotion business, and the assessment results are incorporated into the overall performance assessment of these employees and are linked to their performance bonuses and promotions. In case an employee is proven to have non-compliant behavior, the Group will take graded actions based on the severity of the

The Group follows the relevant content on whistleblowing channels, handling process, and whistleblower protection provisions in the CMS Anti-Fraud Management Policy , establishing a whistleblowing mechanism with clear responsibilities and smooth processes to ensure that every whistleblowing case is handled in a timely and proper closed-loop manner. The Group encourages all employees, partners, customers, suppliers, and other stakeholders to monitor and report any suspected illegal and improper business practices by any personnel.

The Group accepts whistleblowing submissions from a variety of channels, both in real name and anonymously, and has established a systematic process for whistleblowing handling, and the whistleblowing content may be submitted to the Audit Committee under the Board of Directors for review as requested by the whistleblower.
Conduct a detailed intake registration, and securely retain the whistleblowing materials and all forms of evidence.
Verification of information: After whistleblowing is accepted, the content of the whistleblowing and information will be verified and evaluated.

Case investigation: If the report meets the criteria for case filing and investigation, a case will be opened and an investigation will be initiated. The investigation team will be designated at the appropriate level based on the position of the person being reported, and the investigation results will be documented. Based on the principle of avoidance, the person being reported shall not participate in the antifraud investigation against him/her as an investigator. If the person being reported is a member of senior management, the Board of Directors will directly designate a department/person or set up an investigation team to conduct the investigation.

Approval of results: After verification, the investigation records will be submitted to the management or the Board of Directors of the Group for review. The whistleblowing case will be handled strictly in accordance with the evaluation results, and will be announced within the Group.
