Within 3 working days after the completion of the handling, the handling department will proactively provide feedback to the whistleblower orally or in writing, or in other proper forms.
After the conclusion of the whistleblowing review or investigation, the relevant whistleblowing materials shall be filed by the investigator in charge, and archived as confidential documents.
After the process is completed, remedial measures are taken in a timely manner to reassess the situation of the affected business unit, and implement corresponding improvement measures.

The Group has established a strict whistleblower protection mechanism, committed to safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests of whistleblowers. Anonymous whistleblowings are accepted, and the whistleblower' s personal information and whistleblowing content will be kept confidential throughout the entire process. The whistleblower' s identity will not be disclosed without the whistleblower' s consent.

In the case that any handling personnel intentionally discloses the whistleblower' s information or the whistleblowing content, or takes a negative and negligent attitude towards the reported matter, or fails to respond to the whistleblower' s reasonable request for protection when the whistleblower is concerned about retaliation or unfair treatment, the whistleblower may directly report that to the Board of Directors. The Group will take disciplinary action against the relevant personnel in accordance with the seriousness of the violation. In addition, the Group strictly prohibits any form of harassment, harm and retaliation against the whistleblower, and such actions will be dealt with severely once discovered and verified.

The Group strictly adheres to the Cybersecurity Law of the People' s Republic of China, the Data Security Law of the People' s Republic of China , the Personal Information Protection Law of the People' s Republic of China , and other relevant laws and regulations. The Group continuously improves the management systems, strengthens technical safeguards, enhances personnel training, and improves risk prevention capabilities to protect data privacy and security. At the same time, the Group actively embraces the rapid development of digital transformation and artificial intelligence (AI) technology. In the vigorous promotion of AI technology application and innovation, the Group places great emphasis on data governance and ethical compliance construction related to it. The Group continuously strengthens the full-process supervision of AI system data usage and output results, ensuring that technology applications operate within a compliance framework, comprehensively safeguarding the data privacy rights of both internal and third-party entities. During the Reporting Period, the Group did not experience any incidents of customer information and privacy breaches.

The Group has established a systematic information security management framework and formulated internal management systems such as the CMS Regulations on Data Security Management and the CMS Rules on Data Access Management , specifying requirements for data classification and grading, access control, and emergency response. During the Reporting Period, the management regulations for the application of emerging technologies such as AI were updated in the CMS Regulations on Personal Information Protection , providing a solid foundation for comprehensively strengthening the defense of information security and privacy protection.

During the Reporting Period, the Group updated the Cybersecurity Classified Protection Level 3 certification of the Group' s official website. The internal information system has initiated the Cybersecurity Classified Protection Level 2 certification and obtained certification in February 2026. The Group will continuously improve its privacy protection and information security management system by gradually referring to the ISO 27001 standard for information security management systems.

The Group' s privacy protection and information security work is implemented under a tiered governance structure led by the Board of Directors. The Board of Directors, as the highest supervisory body, is responsible for overseeing the Group s privacy protection and information security management and implementation matters, including the latest work progress, audit results, risk identification, and improvement situations. During the Reporting Period, the ESG Committee under the Board of Directors of the Company has reviewed the work of the Group related to privacy protection and information security.

At the implementation level, the Group has appointed the head of the IT Department as the person in charge of cybersecurity at the Group level and the IT Department of the Group is responsible for building, maintaining, and implementing the information security management system, and steadily improving regulations on information security management and data access management. Relying on the internal IT service ticket system, the IT Department will be responsible for responding to and handling service tickets submitted by employees and reporting to the person in charge of cybersecurity for overall management. For major information security issues, the person in charge of cybersecurity will report to the Management Committee of the Group.

The Group has systematically established and implemented privacy protection and information security management measures that cover both internal and external collaboration:

Hierarchical Management | The Group has adopted measures such as internal document separation, document encryption, and data classification management, and has established an operating mechanism and rules for review, approval and authorization for access to customer information. Employees are required to strictly access, query and maintain personal and customer data with authorization, and unauthorized employees are not permitted to use, export or copy any customer information. Access Inspection | The Group regularly inspects the information system access, including but not limited to the authorization mechanism, process, user access, access scope confirmation for in- service employees, and access clearance for departing employees. During the Reporting Period, the Group conducted an annual information system access inspection for internal office system cloud platform to ensure the reasonableness of access settings and security of the relevant data. Confidentiality Management | The Group signs confidentiality agreements with employees, conveying and emphasizing the importance of confidentiality responsibilities and the legal consequences of breach. Employees are encouraged to prevent, stop, and report all related violations through channels such as telephone, email, and internal work software. For confidential data or personal information, sensitive information is desensitized. External Collaboration | For suppliers who may have access to private information of consumers, the Group strictly constrains supplier behavior through contractual agreements, to protect customers' rights related to privacy and personal information.

text: The Group has established a regular internal audit mechanism for information security and privacy protection management, conducting periodic self-inspections and special reviews on information security to systematically identify and prevent potential risks. The Group relies on firewall cybersecurity systems and multiple information security risk alert systems to provide real-time detection and effective alerts for network anomalies, data backups, and equipment anomalies, etc. During the Reporting Period, the Group completed the self-inspection on information security risks and the special internal IT audit. Furthermore, the audit scope was extended to the supply chain, conducting an annual audit of network service providers. This comprehensive evaluation of suppliers covered aspects such as information security management standards, data access, cybersecurity, digital management, and hardware configuration, ensuring both internal and external coordination meet the Group' s high security standards.
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

The Group also enhances the reliability of information security and privacy protection through external information security audits. Since 2021, the Group has engaged an independent third party with professional qualifications for five consecutive years to conduct annual audits, including vulnerability scanning and information asset security reviews, and has conducted simulated hacker attack tests to identify information security and privacy protection risks. When selecting the auditing institution, the Group conducts a comprehensive assessment of its technical team, professional certifications, and market ranking. During the Reporting Period, the Group received 4 information security audits from upstream partners.

Based on the results of internal and external audits and reviews, the Group timely formulates the corresponding preventive measures, and implements targeted upgrading for the information security protection system to sufficiently prevent and resist the relevant risks.

The Group has systematically integrated AI governance into the data compliance and information security management system. During the Reporting Period, the Group further incorporated personal information protection requirements in AI applications into the CMS Regulations on Personal Information Protection , clarifying internal ethical guidelines and technical specifications. This aims to build a secure, trustworthy, and responsible AI application ecosystem, promoting the coordinated development of technology empowerment and compliance governance.

In the application of AI, the Group consistently adheres to the fundamental principles of 'legality, transparency, and trustworthiness,' and continuously strengthens AI governance through systematic management initiatives. When deploying AI tools in the business, the Group informs users through clear means such as interface prompts and privacy policy explanations, ensuring their right to be informed and their right to autonomous choice. In terms of data processing, the Group strictly adheres to the principles of purpose limitation and data minimization, and performs de-identification of personal information. For third-party AI tools and services, the Group implements strict access assessments and continuous supervision to ensure their personal information processing activities comply with the Group' s compliance requirements and relevant laws and regulations.

The Group adheres to fair, impartial, and non-discriminatory AI ethical standards, regularly reviewing and evaluating the AI tools used to identify and mitigate potential algorithmic biases. This ensures that the Group' s AI applications do not produce unjust outcomes based on gender, race, age, health status, religious beliefs, specific identities, and other factors.

The Group continuously strengthens the security risk awareness and compliance behavior capabilities of all employees through a systematic privacy protection and information security training system. Since 2019, the Group has provided all employees with annual training regarding privacy protection and information security for seven consecutive years. During the Reporting Period, the Group conducted information security training covering topics such as data leakage prevention, privacy confidentiality, and information security practices, supplemented by online tests to reinforce learning outcomes. New employees are also required to complete specialized information security training upon joining to ensure they establish the correct protective awareness. Meanwhile, the Group also actively organizes specialized training for information security related technicians. During the Reporting Period, the Group organized trainings on system development and other professional skills for the employees of the IT Department.
Coverage of Privacy Protection and Information Security Training Employees (incl. interns) 90%

Other than regular training, the Group also issues a monthly information security bulletin to all employees, promptly sharing updates on internal and external policy developments and representative cases. In addition, the Group conducts thematic briefings and communications from time to time on topics such as the ISO 27001 standard and laws and regulations on personal information protection. Through diverse forms and continuous penetration, the Group continuously enhances employees' ability to prevent, identify, and respond to information security incidents, laying a solid foundation for building a robust security culture.

To ensure a rapid and effective response in the event of an information security incident, the Group has established a regular emergency drill mechanism. According to the CMS Emergency Plan for Information Security Incidents and other policies, the Group conducts at least one special drill annually to continuously optimize internal risk control and collaborative response capabilities. During the Reporting Period, the Group completed two system recovery drills. By simulating scenarios such as sudden failures of business systems, the Group actually initiated the emergency disaster recovery process to verify system recovery efficiency and business continuity assurance levels, effectively enhancing the team' s practical capabilities and strengthening the information security defense line.

The Group strictly complies with the relevant laws and regulations on intellectual property protection in the countries and regions where it operates. By formulating the CMS Intellectual Property Management Policy, the Group has clearly defined the management requirements for the protection of intellectual property such as trademarks, patents, copyrights, and trade secrets. The Group identifies and assesses intellectual property risks in different business scenarios, integrating control plans with processes, policies, and standards to improve intellectual property management and risk assessment. During the Reporting Period, the Group did not experience any significant intellectual property infringement litigation cases.

The Group has established an intellectual property management system that encompasses the entire process of product investment, development, registration, promotion, and sales. Through systematic construction and continuous improvement of the internal 'Intellectual Property Archive Database,' the Group conducts unified filing and dynamic maintenance of assets such as trademarks, patents, and copyrights, laying the foundation for systematic management of intellectual property. The Group matches corresponding legal risk control mechanisms and embeds intellectual property review and compliance checkpoints in each key business process. At the same time, the Group regularly monitors the legal status of intellectual property and the market environment to ensure the continuous effectiveness of assets and prevent potential infringement risks.

The Group incorporates intellectual property protection into the scope of internal control system, regularly assesses and identifies the risk points in the acquisition, maintenance and renewal of intellectual property on a yearly basis, and optimizes the management measures accordingly. By actively monitoring industry trends and feedback from business departments on suspected infringement activities, the Group focuses on intellectual property risk situations. The Group' s Legal Department conducts rapid assessments of potential risks and initiates response procedures. If infringement is confirmed, the Group will, as appropriate, utilize administrative or judicial avenues to safeguard its legitimate rights and interests. In addition, the Group has initially established a special anti-counterfeiting action plan and will make dynamic adjustments during business operations.

While protecting its own intellectual property rights, the Group also regards respecting others' intellectual property rights as an important component of compliant operations and social responsibility. The Group complies with relevant domestic and international laws and regulations by embedding intellectual property reviews in various business processes to systematically avoid potential infringement risks. To actively accept social supervision, the Group has opened multiple channels of complaint to the public. Any individual or organization that discovers any infringement by the Group can file a complaint or report through email, phone, or the official website. The Group will promptly accept, investigate, and rectify the issue.

The Group has established a systematic training system focused on key positions. The Group engages external experts to conduct customized courses for the pharmaceutical industry, covering areas such as patent protection for drugs, overseas patent strategy, protection of technical secrets, continuously enhancing the team' s professional response capabilities and risk control levels in industry-specific scenarios.

The Group adheres to the mission of 'offering competitive products and services to meet unmet medical needs' , consistently prioritizing patient safety and public health. The Group systematically builds and continuously improves a full-cycle quality management system that covers research and development, production, distribution, and post-market surveillance. The Group ensures product quality through stringent research and development and production controls, safeguarding medication safety with proactive pharmacovigilance and an efficient product recall mechanism, thereby creating sustainable health value for patients and society.

The Group strictly complies with the laws and regulations regarding product quality, labeling instructions, complaint response, pharmacovigilance, and product recalls in all operational locations. The Group has established a quality management system that covers the entire process from clinical research and development, registration and evaluation, manufacturing management, marketing authorization, and post-market surveillance. The Group also leverages the digital drug traceability and pharmacovigilance system to comprehensively control the risks related to product quality and safety.

The Group continuously improves its quality assurance mechanism, which covers key aspects such as risk identification and control, safety assessment, complaint management, product recall, change management, deviation management, corrective and preventive action management, and supplier management, through regular internal and external reviews. During the Reporting Period, the Group did not record any material non-compliance with applicable laws or provisions that would significantly impact the Group in product quality and safety, pharmacovigilance, product recall, package inserts and labels management, etc.

To continuously strengthen the quality culture construction throughout the product life cycle, the Group further optimized the systematic and hierarchical training system during the Reporting Period. Through the internal online learning platform, the Group precisely delivered three batches of quality and safety courses to all employees. The content covered core areas such as Good Supply Practice

R&D quality is the foundation of innovation and the basis of safety. On the basis of strict compliance with relevant national laws and regulations and as guided by industry standards such as the Good Clinical Practice (GCP), the Group has established a quality control system for research and development, covering clinical trial, quality assurance and pharmacovigilance. This ensures scientific rigor and process reliability, laying a solid foundation for the safe market launch of products.

To improve the internal product research and development quality management system and standard work processes, the Group formulated the CMS Management Standards for Compliance in Clinical Research . During the Reporting Period, the Medical Department introduced several internal policies, including the Clinical Trial Drug Management Procedures , to continuously optimize the Group' s clinical research-related work, including clinical operations, quality assurance, medical strategy, and pharmacovigilance.

The Group continuously enhances its digital management capabilities to empower R&D quality construction. It completes the online approval of clinical trial protocols through internal work platforms and introduces external systems to standardize the collection of key data during the research process. This strengthens the transparency and traceability of project management throughout the entire process, further ensuring the reliability of R&D quality and data.

The Group has established a dual R&D quality assurance mechanism that combines internal process control with external expert supervision. The Group, through its Medical Department, has systematically constructed a comprehensive R&D quality management closed-loop covering product evaluation, trial design, clinical operation, statistical analysis of trial data, and archive management for clinical reports. Based on the type and complexity of clinical trials, the Group develops audit plans for the corresponding projects through prospective risk assessments and performs inspections at different stages of clinical trials, so as to dynamically identify potential risks and implement timely rectification, and to ensure that various clinical trials fully comply with the requirements of national regulations and industry norms.

Moreover, the Group has engaged experts in quality, medicine, and medication safety fields as consultants to review and check the construction of its internal quality system and actively conducted targeted improvements to enhance the effectiveness of quality control over product research and development.
Protection of Rights and Interests of Clinical Trial Subjects

The Group strictly adheres to the ethical guidelines for clinical trials, following the ethical principles of the Declaration of Helsinki and relevant regulatory requirements, consistently prioritizing the protection of the rights and interests of trial subjects. All human clinical trials of the Group are conducted after obtaining approvals from the drug administration authorities and having passed ethical reviews. Before participating in a clinical trial, all subjects are required to sign the Informed Consent Form of Subjects, which clearly stipulates that they shall have the right to be informed and the freedom to choose, and that they have the right to refuse or withdraw from the clinical trial at any time, thereby protecting their rights and interests.
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

The Group has established a research and development quality inspection system that combines departmental self-inspection, internal audit within the Group, and external inspections, continuously strengthening the ability to prevent and control quality risks. The Group' s Medical Department follows the Operating Procedures for Clinical Trial Inspection, conducting regular self-inspections of ongoing clinical projects annually, identifying areas for improvement, implementing corrective measures, and producing inspection reports. Meanwhile, the Group also conducts internal audits on clinical research projects, covering research documents, processes, and safety risks, etc., and continuously enhances its ability to prevent and control quality risks in research and development process based on the audit results. In addition, the Group also accepts external inspections from cooperative partners and the National Medical Products Administration on the Group' s research and development quality management system and the implementation of product clinical trials.

During the Reporting Period, the Group completed 9 internal audits and 3 external inspections related to clinical trail quality. No significant quality risks in research and development and no serious deficiencies were noted in the relevant internal audits and external inspections.

The Group has established a systematic clinical R&D quality-specific training system. Through internal and external collaboration and empowerment, the Group continuously enhances the team' s professional capabilities and project execution standards, building an internally and externally coordinated, fully controlled clinical research quality ecosystem.

For internal employees, the Group organizes tiered and categorized training: On one hand, through frequent internal training, the Group conducted over 20 sessions throughout the year on standard operating procedures (SOP), regulations, and project processes, covering all members of the medical team. Additionally, the Group relied on the knowledge base of the Medical Department to achieve centralized management and sharing of standard documents, strengthening the consistency of process implementation. On the other hand, the Group organized employees participating in clinical research projects to complete the GCP training at the Advanced Study Institute of the National Medical Products Administration.

At the same time, the Group has extended R&D quality management training to partners. The project team conducts targeted training for suppliers, covering core standards such as GCP requirements and data integrity, to ensure their operations are in sync with the Company' s R&D quality system. During the Reporting Period, the Group conducted 4 R&D quality management training sessions for suppliers.

The Group regards product quality and safety as the foundation of corporate sustainable development and has established a quality management system covering the entire value chain. Through an annual system review and dynamic revision mechanism, the Group ensures that the management system consistently complies with the latest regulations and industry requirements. It has formulated the CMS Management Provisions on the Direct Reporting of Quality Information to clarify the responsibilities of each business unit and the information reporting procedures, thus forming an efficient and transparent quality risk prevention and communication channel.

In terms of product sourcing and standards control, the drug products promoted and sold by the Group are mainly produced by original manufacturers (suppliers) located in China, Germany, Denmark, the United Kingdom and France, in which the manufacturers are in strict compliance with the production quality management regulations of the countries where the drugs are produced. A small portion of the products are self-produced (during the Reporting Period, the sales contribution from self-produced products accounted for only approximately 0.7 % of the Group' s turnover in the case that all medicines were directly sold by the Group). All drugs promoted and sold by the Group have been registered and approved by relevant drug administration authorities (e.g., China NMPA).

To ensure the effective operation of the quality management system, the Group has established a regular internal and external supervision mechanism. In accordance with internal audit regulations such as the Regulations on Internal Audit of Quality Management System and the Operating Procedures for Internal Audit of Quality Management System , the Group organizes comprehensive internal audits and special inspections covering business and production processes annually. During the Reporting Period, the Group completed 1 special audit and 2 annual audits on quality management among the product operations-related departments, as well as 8 self-inspections of manufacturing-related departments on the production quality management system, to ensure that the quality assurance and risk control procedures of the Group are effectively implemented. Moreover, the Group has formulated corresponding corrective and preventive measures to address the relevant issues, and the correction has been successfully completed as planned. Meanwhile, the Group has accepted and successfully passed the supervisory inspections from external regulatory authorities. During the Reporting Period, the Group accepted and successfully passed 1 supervisory inspection from drug administration authorities, concerning the quality management of drug promotion and sales as well as manufacturing. No major risks or severe defects concerning product quality were identified.
Quality and Safety Management of Self-produced Products

For the self-produced products, the Group' s manufacturing subsidiary has established a quality control system covering material supply, product manufacturing, release testing, market release and use, product recall, and other core operational aspects. The Group' s manufacturing subsidiary has complied with the GMP, and has obtained the GB/T 19001-2016/ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management System certification.

In terms of source control, the Group has established a strict material selection mechanism. The Group dynamically updates the list of qualified suppliers through implementing hierarchical management, on-site audits, and annual performance reviews of suppliers. For key material suppliers who have significant impacts on drug quality and medication safety, the Group arranges on-site inspections and quality audits on a yearly basis, prioritizing the materials provided by qualified suppliers with high comprehensive scores to ensure the quality of raw materials from the source. In addition, for all incoming materials, the Group conducts strict incoming inspection by checking the appearance of materials and verifying material-related information, etc. The Group also conducts sampling inspection according to the Sampling Management Procedures, and releases the materials for production after they are accepted as qualified, with a traceable material information database to refine the material control process.
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

During the product manufacturing process, the Group performs regular calibration and maintenance of production equipment, and assigns dedicated personnel to monitor and record key process parameters throughout the entire process. The Group thoroughly inspects each batch of products to ensure the products are qualified and well-packed before entering the market. For specific products, samples are taken in strict accordance with national standards to test stability before delivery, to ensure that product quality aligns with national pharmaceutical standards.

The Group has established a regular quality review and improvement mechanism. According to the established Product Quality Review and Analysis Management Procedure, the Group summarizes and analyzes all data related to production and quality inspection on a yearly basis, including but not limited to quality training, deviation analysis, product return and recall, complaints and adverse drug reaction reports, etc. Through this mechanism, the Group is able to proactively identify potential trends and risks, take corrective and preventive measures in a timely manner, and drive the quality management system to achieve closed-loop optimization. During the Reporting Period, the Group completed the quality review and analysis for the previous year' s self-produced products and confirmed that the key technological parameters were stable and controllable, and the product quality consistently satisfied the standards.

To strengthen the internal awareness of product quality, the Group regards production quality as one of the factors in evaluating the operation targets of production-related departments and conducts quality target assessment at least once a year. According to the Quality Policy, Target, and Plan Management Regulations , the Group includes the product qualification rate, the evaluation score for production equipment maintenance, and the quality training completion rate into the annual performance assessment of employees. This ensures a close connection between quality targets and individual performance. A quality management team, composed of heads of production-related departments, inspects the achievement of quality targets of each entity.

In addition, the Group continuously enhances the professional capabilities and sense of responsibility of production personnel by conducting specialized training on quality management standards, operating procedures, and quality awareness. During the Reporting Period, the Group' s manufacturing subsidiary conducted quality-related training for employees in accordance with the annual training plan.
Quality and Safety Management of Finished Products

The Group' s subsidiaries involved in business operations have all complied with the GSP, and strictly complied with relevant regulations regarding drug promotion and sales and manufacturing to ensure product quality and medication safety.

During the quality admission and acceptance process, the Group strictly inspects finished products in accordance with national product standards or product quality standards approved by the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA). For imported drug products, the Group strictly follows the requirements of national laws and regulations and undergoes stringent inspections by the Institute for Food and Drug Control, including the first batch of imported drugs, biological products, products after standard change or manufacturing process alteration, etc., and may require issuing the Import Inspection Report as necessary. Upon the arrival of the imported and domestic drug products, the Quality Management Department of the corresponding subsidiaries in drug operation business of the Group will conduct batch-by-batch inspections as per GSP requirements, and verify the product inspection reports. In case of any product quality issues, the Group will handle the problematic products by isolating, reporting, returning, or destroying them in accordance with the Operating Procedures for Reporting and Confirming Unqualified Drugs and the Operating Procedures for Destruction of Unqualified Drugs , ensuring that unqualified products never enter the market. In addition, the Group has established an independent special drug safety management system to implement stricter compliance management controls for specific products.

To safeguard the safety and stability of marketed drugs' quality, the Group has established a regular post-marketing monitoring and review mechanism. The Group regularly conducts post-market evaluations on the safety, efficacy and quality controllability of drugs, proactively identifying and controlling risks. At the same time, according to the Operating Procedures for Internal Audit of Quality Management System , the Quality Management Department of relevant responsible subsidiaries of the Group conducts an annual review of the quality safety and supply stability of historical product acceptance, forming an Annual Product Inbound Quality Review Form , which shall be reviewed and approved by the designated quality responsible person and then filed for recordkeeping.

The Group attaches great importance to the warehousing and storage safety of products, and has formulated the Regulations on Drug Storage, the Regulations on Warehouse Handling Area Working Safety Management, the Regulations on Warehouse Hygiene, the Regulations on Inspection, Maintenance and Servicing of Equipment and Facilities, the Regulations on Drug Maintenance and other relevant regulations to ensure that staff on duty understand their responsibilities and work content, and are clear about the warehousing process and handling requirements, while giving comprehensive guidance on fire safety management, hygiene conditions, equipment maintenance and drug maintenance of warehouses.

In terms of warehouse management, the Group assigns maintenance personnel in the warehouse to have real-time monitoring of the condition of equipment and drugs stored in the warehouse in accordance with GSP and management system as well as operating procedures, regularly inspect and maintain facilities and equipment, and quarterly summarize and analyze the drug storage and warehousing status.

For drugs under special control, the Group implements stricter control measures. The Group has formulated regulations on safety management of Diazepam Nasal Spray, which is a psychotropic drug of category II and was approved for marketing in 2023, and has set up separate warehouses for special drugs, with monitoring equipment installed and alarm devices connected to the public security system, in order to enhance the quality and safety management of drugs. For products that require refrigeration, the Group has set up independent refrigeration warehouses managed by designated personnel, equipped with essential hardware facilities, a round-the-clock automatic temperature and humidity monitoring system, etc., as well as emergency generators and emergency management plans to safeguard the quality and safety of drugs.

During the transportation process, the Group strictly implements cold chain and temperature-controlled logistics standards. The Group uses professional refrigerated vehicles or insulation equipment and packaging to ensure that products are delivered within the required temperature range.

The Group has formulated the Drug Traceability Management Policy and established a complete product information database within the computer system in compliance with GSP requirements by utilizing the electronic traceability code. The electronic traceability code on a drug packaging box provides a unique traceable mark for the minimum saleable packaging unit, which realizes information-based traceability of the minimum saleable packaging unit of drugs, ensuring that the drugs can be 'traced back to their origin and destination' and providing more effective and comprehensive quality control support for the procurement, storage, sale and transportation of the drugs.

In addition, the Group actively promotes the social collaboration of traceability information and has been enrolled in the 'Mashangfangxin Platform' to share drug traceability information with its downstream customers and relevant parties in the industry, thereby enhancing the ability to ensure patient medication safety.

The Group strictly abides by the laws and regulations such as the Provisions for Package Inserts and Labels and has established relevant internal management policies and procedures such as the Procedure for Administration of Drafting/Alteration of Package Inserts and Labels and Procedure for Revision, Review, and Approval of Package Inserts and Labels, so as to clearly define control requirements on drafting, altering, revising, reviewing and approving product package inserts and labels.

The Group' s Registration Management Department is responsible for leading the drafting and revision of package inserts and labels. In the event of updates of relevant laws and regulations, approval of drug marketing applications, re-registration and other changes related to package inserts and labels, the Registration Management Department of the Group will evaluate the type of change based on the relevant laws and regulations and initiate the corresponding drafting or revision process accordingly. For changes that require reporting, the Registration Management Department will organize an internal review and submit a supplementary application or filing to the regulatory authorities in accordance with procedures. If any such change only requires submission in the annual report, it will be included in the drug annual report as stipulated. After the supplementary application or filing is approved or publicly announced by the regulatory authorities, the Registration Management Department will complete the corresponding revisions of the package inserts and labels based on the approval or announcement. After review, approval and release by the department head and relevant partners, the revised package inserts and labels will be officially put into use.

The Group places great emphasis on the medication safety of the public and, guided by risk minimization, it has established a systematic, full-chain pharmacovigilance (PV) management system. The Group strictly complies with laws and regulations, industry guidelines and other requirements, continuously optimizes the pharmacovigilance system covering drug research and development and post-marketing products. Simultaneously, the Group has established and improved product recall management systems, operating procedures, and handling plans, and comprehensively deployed and implemented quality and safety assessment, and risk identification and control throughout the entire product lifecycle from research and development to post-marketing use.

The Group has established a pharmacovigilance system covering the entire lifecycle of drugs, systematically constructing a safety risk management mechanism from clinical development to post-marketing stages. The Group has established diverse adverse event feedback channels, strictly implements standardized safety event handling procedures, and continuously conducts pharmacovigilance training for all employees, and effectively fulfills corporate responsibility to safeguard patient medication safety.

The Group strictly adheres to the Good Pharmacovigilance Practice, the Measures for Reporting and Monitoring of Adverse Drug Reactions and other relevant national laws and regulations, and continuously improves its management system of pre-marketing and post-marketing pharmacovigilance, which includes the Pharmacovigilance Quality Management Regulations, the Emergency Plan for Drug Safety Incidents, the Operating Procedures for Cluster Adverse Drug Reaction Events , and other internal regulations.

The Group has established a clear hierarchical pharmacovigilance regulatory framework, covering three types of documents: regulations, responsibilities, and operating procedures. This framework systematically regulates aspects such as system establishment and maintenance, drug risk identification and assessment, adverse reaction monitoring and reporting, training and record-keeping, internal audits and quality management, as well as personnel requirements. The system spans the entire process from drug approval to the cancellation of the approval number. It is continuously optimized through regular internal audits and training mechanisms, forming a closed loop of prevention, identification, control, and communication.

Based on the established the Drug Safety Committee Management Regulations , the relevant subsidiaries of the Group have established Drug Safety Committees to oversee the pharmacovigilance of drugs on sale and the effectiveness of the safety risk control system. Through a regular working mechanism, the Drug Safety Committees conduct systematic monitoring and dynamic assessment of drug safety risks, and based on the assessment results, promote the formulation and implementation of risk control measures. In addition to routine duty performance, the Committees hold regular meetings annually to comprehensively review the annual pharmacovigilance work report and the effectiveness of risk control measures. This ensures that the drug safety management system continuously complies with regulatory requirements and business development needs, enabling the Group to effectively fulfill its primary responsibility for drug safety.

The Group has established a systematic drug safety risk management mechanism covering the entire lifecycle of drugs. For products at the clinical development stage, the Group continuously monitors and identifies the safety risks throughout the entire research and development process of drugs and regularly prepares the R&D Safety Update Report every year to optimize the clinical medication safety risk prevention and management strategies dynamically. In addition, for commercialized products, the Group prepares the Periodic Drug Safety Update Report and the Pharmacovigilance Plan for each drug to continuously analyze and proactively prevent potential risks, thereby achieving a closed-loop management process from monitoring, assessment to intervention.

Through regular internal and external audits, the Group continuously improves its drug safety risk management efforts. During the Reporting Period, the Group conducted 1 internal audit on departments in relation to pharmacovigilance, and accepted and successfully passed 2 external audits from product suppliers. The audit results indicated that no significant risks or serious deficiencies related to pharmacovigilance were identified within the Group.

The Group has established diverse channels for collecting information on adverse product events, including telephone, email, official website, and internal communication platforms, etc., so that internal and external stakeholders can provide timely feedback to the Group and contact the relevant personnel in charge when problems arise during the use of drugs. In the meantime, the Group proactively accesses and collects information on suspected adverse drug reactions from the public's spontaneous reports, clinical applications, post-marketing clinical studies, academic literature, etc., to achieve effective monitoring of product safety information.

Upon receipt of suspected adverse reactions/events and other safety information of the products, the pharmacovigilance-related departments of the Group will follow the Operating Procedures for Postmarketing Individual Case Safety Reports and the Operating Procedures for Cluster Adverse Drug Reaction Events to collect information, conduct investigation, analysis, handling, assessment and summarization on individual adverse reactions/events, and timely and truthfully record the information via the digital pharmacovigilance system, ensuring truthful reporting to regulatory authorities within the stipulated time limit.

The Group strictly complies with relevant laws, regulations and management procedures and has established the Regulations on Supplier Management, Regulations on Hierarchical Supplier Management, the Regulations on First-time Supplier Qualification Review, the Provisions for Material Supplier Management and other internal regulations and policies to achieve full-process risk monitoring and management from admission, cooperation, to eventual exit, by means of admission review, hierarchical management, regular evaluation and assessment, etc., thereby continuously building a more resilient and sustainable industrial ecosystem.

During the Reporting Period, 100% of the Group' s finished product and material suppliers were managed in full compliance with the aforementioned standards. There was no significant delay of products or materials from the Group' s suppliers. Additionally, the Group's Audit Department conducted 2 targeted audits on the internal control procedures pertaining to finished goods procurement, material procurement, and import/export operations. Neither significant supply chain management risks nor serious deficiencies were noted from the relevant audit work.

The Group continuously optimizes the management of material suppliers by implementing comprehensive whole-process management from admission to exit, promptly identifying and controlling potential risks at each stage, thereby ensuring material quality.

At the stage of admission of material suppliers, the Group conducts a comprehensive admission review of potential suppliers through transparent and fair bidding, including the suppliers' scales, qualifications, operational status, production capacities, product categories, quality management, reputation history, conditions of transportation, etc., so as to ensure the standardization of supplier admission.

During the preliminary supplier review stage, the Group also collects the Manufacturer Questionnaire for more efficient communications and decision-making. Before concluding a cooperation agreement with a supplier, the Quality Management Department of the Group will lead the qualification review and conduct an on-site quality audit, which mainly focuses on materials that have a significant impact on the drug quality and safety. In the meantime, the Group conducts stringent testing on the samples provided by the supplier according to the material procurement management requirements, and conducts a small batch trial production when necessary. After the supplier undergoes a complete review process and is assessed and approved by the Quality Management Department, it will be included in the Group' s list of qualified material suppliers.

The Group implements hierarchical management for qualified suppliers according to the impact of their materials on product quality and safety. According to the Provisions for Material Supplier Management and the relationship between materials and key product quality, suppliers are classified into Grade I (primary/non-primary) suppliers and Grade II suppliers. Among them, Grade I suppliers provide materials that directly affect the key quality of products (such as raw and auxiliary materials, and packaging materials in direct contact with products), while Grade II suppliers provide materials that indirectly affect quality (such as external packaging materials, and testing reagents).
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

The Quality Management Department of the Group conducts annual quality assessment on key material suppliers regularly, utilizing a comprehensive approach that includes qualification audits, sample testing, on-site audits, and document audits to perform multidimensional evaluations. Special emphasis is placed on conducting on-site quality audits for suppliers of primary raw and auxiliary materials, as well as internal packaging materials. During the Reporting Period, the Group completed on-site audits for 23 material suppliers.

Based on the assessment scores, a comprehensive supplier score is formed to achieve differentiated risk management. Suppliers with a comprehensive material supplier evaluation score of 70 or above, who have completed the rectification of deficiencies identified during the assessment process, may be considered as qualified suppliers for the Company once their rectification documentation or plans are submitted and verified. The higher the comprehensive evaluation score, the longer the supplier assessment cycle may be appropriately extended.

If a supplier is found to be unqualified during a quality re-inspection, the Group will issue a nonconformity report and inform the supplier in time to return of the unqualified goods. Suppliers who fail to meet the Group's requirements twice in a year will be disqualified. If goods are found with any severe defect or significant quality risks, the Group will suspend procurement from this supplier to prevent and reduce quality risks. In addition, for suppliers with a comprehensive score below 70 points, and who still do not meet the requirements after reassessment following rectification, the Group will also terminate cooperation with them. During the Reporting Period, the Group terminated cooperation with 3 suppliers.

Meanwhile, to minimize or avoid supply chain risks resulting from material shortages, the Group has reserved backup suppliers for critical materials to address potential emergencies and ensure supply stability.

Shenzhen Kangzhe, a subsidiary of the Group mainly responsible for importing and distributing pharmaceutical products, is certified as an advanced 'Authorized Economic Operator (AEO)' by the customs, which represents a high level of integrated supply chain management and excellent internal governance and cross-border trade safety control under internationally recognized standards.

The Group has formulated a series of internal policies, such as the Admission and Evaluation System of Suppliers , and adheres to a stringent admission review mechanism for its suppliers. The review comprehensively covers key dimensions such as company qualification and scale, competitiveness, production status, corporate reputation, product quality management, logistics and transportation capacity, customer service, environmental protection, and social responsibility. Through this mechanism, the Group can systematically screen and introduce high-quality suppliers with legitimate qualifications, excellent quality and social responsibility, ensuring compliance, stability, and sustainability of the supply chain from the source.

The Group has newly introduced the Regulations on Hierarchical Supplier Management . For new suppliers and stable suppliers, the Group conducts important scoring and hierarchical management according to quantitative indicators such as the annual procurement amount, the proportion of procurement amount to suppliers' revenue as well as suppliers' performance levels. Suppliers are categorized into four types: partner suppliers, key commercial suppliers, prior suppliers and commercial suppliers, achieving differentiated management of suppliers.

The Group regularly conducts comprehensive audits of suppliers. Among them, for partner and key commercial suppliers, the Group conducts a risk assessment once a year. For prior and commercial suppliers, an assessment is conducted every 18 months. The assessment covers the aspects of qualification, operational risk, product pricing, operational procedures and performance, and service quality, etc. If higher risks are identified, the Group will communicate and convene regular meetings with suppliers to actively explore solutions, assist suppliers in developing response plans, and continuously monitor and reduce supply risks.

The Group strictly implements supplier quality management. The Supply Chain Management Department of the Group and relevant departments jointly implement strict inspection on qualification report and receipt for imported and domestic finished products to ensure that the products meet the national quality standards. Once any quality problem is found, the Group will immediately gain an in-depth understanding of the causes, provide feedback to the suppliers, urge them to rectify and provide necessary supports. If a supplier fails a sampling inspection conducted by an institute for drug control or has any major quality issues, is subject to a recall order, or has a poor quality reputation, etc., the Group' s Quality Management Department will organize on-site visits, make an all-round risk assessment, and focus on the supplier' s quality management system and the effectiveness of the supplier' s corrective measures. For suppliers assessed as unqualified, the Group will terminate the cooperation with them in accordance with the supplier exit mechanism to ensure the product quality.

The Group has established a supply assurance strategy centered on proactive management. Based on scientific supply and demand analysis and a cross-departmental coordination mechanism, the Group forecasts and assesses business objectives to drive the formulation of forward-looking procurement plans, thereby reducing the risk of supply fluctuations. At the same time, the Group has established a dynamic monitoring and rapid response mechanism. In response to market demand fluctuations, changes in production capacity, or external environmental uncertainties, the Group promptly initiates plan adjustment contingencies to continuously support the stable operation of the Group's business.

Sustainable Development of the Supply Chain

The Group deeply integrates the concept of sustainable development into supply chain management, systematically promoting the collaborative development of the industrial chain. The Group considers the environmental and social risks of partners as one of the important factors in cooperation decisions. The Group makes all efforts to identify, monitor and control the environmental and social responsibility risks in different segments of the supply chain, including supplier selection, procurement, production, logistics, import and export, product distribution, etc., so as to continuously promote the development of the supply chain towards a green, low-carbon, and sustainable direction, thereby building a transparent, responsible, and resilient supply chain system.

To guide supply chain partners in practicing sustainable development concepts, the Group has officially formulated the CMS Code of Conduct for Suppliers , advocating that suppliers adhere to the responsibility standards issued by the Group in aspects such as business ethics, product and service quality, labor rights, occupational health and safety, and environmental protection. The code-related documents and complaint channels for violations are publicly available through the official website and other platforms, facilitating stakeholders to supervise the compliance of the Group and suppliers, and jointly promote compliance, integrity, and sustainable development in the supply chain.

The Group systematically integrates sustainable development into supply chain management by identifying and controlling potential social and environmental risks in supplier selection, product procurement and production, and logistics transportation. The Group has established and implemented an ESG risk prevention and control mechanism for the supply chain, promoting suppliers to jointly enhance their sense of responsibility and practice standards, thereby building a resilient and sustainable supply chain system.

Supplier Selection | • Adhering to the principle of openness,fairness and impartiality, preventing and controlling possible corruption risks in the bidding process with participation of multiple departments; • Including human rights, environmental and social factors into the annual supplier assessment and review; encouraging and inclined to choose suppliers advocating the green environmental protection concept or with relevant qualifications, including but not limited to: ISO 14000, ISO 45001, SA8000, AEO, Transported Asset Protection Association (TAPA), etc.; • Under similar objective conditions, prioritizing the supplier that is geographically closer and more easily accessible if the candidates are on a par, in order to reduce the potential environmental pollution during transportation. Procurement and Production | • Clearly stating quality integrity, supply integrity, anti-corruption and other compliance requirements in agreements signed with suppliers, and requiring suppliers to comply with national and industry standards related to product operations and production; • Formulating the Provisions for Material Supplier Management , which clearly defines the scope of supplier audits, including dimensions such as legal operation, product quality, environment and governance; • Requiring suppliers to comply with environmental standards for packaging materials. The inner packaging in contact with drugs is required to be at least the food-grade packaging to realize green packaging. Logistics Transportation | • Conducting all-round assessment in terms of qualification and capacities, to ensure product quality during the distribution process and to minimize the potential impact of goods circulation on the surrounding environment; • Including environmental and social factors in selection criteria for logistics service providers and distributors, including enterprise qualification, warehousing and distribution capacities, staffing, operational management, channel coverage, response efficiency, reputation in the industry and dedication to environmental protection; • Prioritizing distributors with TAPA certification, complying with GSP requirements, larger scale in the sales region, comprehensive distribution channels coverage and dedication to social responsibility and environmental protection; • Making a series of internal management regulations available to logistics service providers and distributors, to ensure that partners are aware of and comply with the Group's requirements and standards for product quality and safety, anti-corruption, intellectual property protection, data privacy protection, compliant employment, and environmental protection; • Adding relevant terms related to anti-corruption, anti-bribery and compliance operation to the cooperation contracts signed with logistics service providers and distributors, requiring logistics service providers and distributors to confirm their compliance with the Group's relevant provisions; • Conducting audits related to the Good Distribution Practice (GDP) for logistics service providers and regularly assessing and improving their operational quality; • Monitoring logistics service providers' environmental management practices and carbon emissions during the logistics processes, and sharing current measures available to control the increase in carbon emissions; • Providing training to international logistics service providers on related topics such as product transportation quality and environmental protection.

text: CMS's Supply Chain ESG Risk Management Initiatives
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

To continuously identify and manage ESG risks in the supply chain, the Group systematically conducted an ESG questionnaire survey for suppliers during the Reporting Period. The survey content covered multiple dimensions, including business ethics, product and service quality assurance, human rights protection, occupational health and safety, and environmental protection, aiming to assess suppliers' actual conditions in ESG policy formulation, management measure implementation, and risk control. This work helps the Group to more comprehensively grasp the ESG performance of the supply chain and provides a basis for subsequent risk management and collaborative improvement.

The Group is committed to promoting integrity and transparency in supply chain management, integrating principles of integrity and compliance into procurement practices. Through a combination of institutional constraints, capacity building, and continuous supervision, the Group systematically builds an ecosystem of honest and transparent business cooperation. The Group explicitly incorporates antibribery and anti-corruption clauses in all supplier agreements and requires them to strictly comply with the laws and regulations of their operating locations. At the same time, through signing the Supplier Initiative Letter , the Group promotes partners' joint commitment to adhere to regulations regarding business ethics, human rights guidelines, environmental protection, and respect for community culture, etc.

To continuously enhance suppliers' compliance awareness, the Group has also established a regular integrity management mechanism: Continuously collecting suppliers' internal anti-corruption policies and regulations to ensure that suppliers have a comprehensive anti-corruption management system, and actively communicating with each supplier regarding the latest anti-corruption requirements and trends in their respective industries. Each subsidiary of the Group conducts annual compliance training for suppliers and distributors through an online platform. In addition, we incorporate the integrity performance of suppliers into the scope of on-site audits, focusing on examining their implementation of relevant regulations and the fulfillment of relevant initiatives, to ensure that integrity responsibilities effectively extend to all aspects of the supply chain.

The Group has established a transparent anti-corruption whistleblowing and feedback mechanism for upstream and downstream partners. Partners can provide feedback via email, telephone contact, official website, face-to-face communication, etc. In the course of cooperation with the Group, partners may conduct whistleblowing either anonymously or with their real names through the aforesaid channels if they find that any employee is involved in irregular behaviors such as bribery and corruption, unfair competition, disclosure of commercial or technical secrets, and abuse of authority. Upon receipt of a whistleblowing submission, the Group' s Supply Management Department will collaborate with the Compliance Department and other relevant units to immediately initiate risk identification, assessment, and investigation procedures within the compliance framework. Special inspections will be conducted as necessary to ensure that all whistleblowing submissions are handled promptly and fairly, thus jointly maintaining a clean and regulated business ecosystem.
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

The Group has established a regular communication mechanism with suppliers, maintaining twoway communication through regular meetings, special topic meetings, and satisfaction surveys across multiple channels. The Group holds regular monthly meetings with core suppliers to promptly summarize cooperation performance and provide feedback on optimization directions. During the Reporting Period, the Group organized themed meetings, such as review meetings, communication meetings and briefing sessions to interact and communicate with suppliers, and clarified the requirements that suppliers should meet in terms of business operations and sustainable development. In addition, the Supply Chain Management Department regularly conducts supplier satisfaction surveys to promote cooperative trust and collaborative improvement with partners.

In terms of training empowerment, the Group has established a systematic training system that covers all suppliers. During the Reporting Period, the Group conducted two rounds of specialized training for all suppliers: First, based on the CMS Code of Conduct for Suppliers , the Group conducted training for all suppliers covering ESG governance requirements, and product and service quality assurance, achieving a 100% supplier training coverage rate; second, the Quality Management Department, in collaboration with the Supply Chain Management Department, conducted quality management training based on the latest internal regulations, covering training content such as drug warehousing management, data integrity, and key operational processes, with a view to continuously enhancing suppliers' compliance operations and comprehensive assurance capabilities.

In addition, the Registration Management Department of the Group proactively initiates training such as product quality standards for suppliers in case of any updates to the registration standards and legal and regulatory requirements, to promptly convey policy interpretations and quality requirements, while formulating clear compliance transition plans in collaboration with suppliers. This ensures that the supply chain smoothly adapts to regulatory changes and continues to meet regulatory requirements.

CMS places great importance on and actively fulfills its social responsibilities, committed to achieving harmonious development between the Company and society. The Group engages in a series of public welfare activities such as disaster relief donations, rural revitalization, caring for vulnerable groups, and supporting education. By doing so, we leverage our influence in the field of social welfare, actively participate in and promote community

development, and contribute to building a harmonious society. During the Reporting Period, the Shenzhen subsidiary of the Group was selected in the '2025 Top 100 Enterprises with the Highest Social Contributions of the Shenzhen Top 500' .

In order to optimize the approval process for public welfare donations and ensure standardized and effective donations, the Group has updated the External Donation Management Policy to truly play a role in promoting community development:
Defining the principles, types and recipients of public donations and corresponding approval procedures;

Requiring that donations and public welfare activities are conducted based on the principles of legality and compliance, sustainability, unified management, honesty and trustworthiness, and continuous tracking;
Defining the project initiation and approval process for external donations, and establishing corresponding approval standards based on the differences in donation types;
Clearly dividing the responsibilities of all relevant departments and systematically managing the Group's external donation behaviors.

During the Reporting Period, the Audit Department of the Group included donation matters within the audit scope for relevant audit projects. The compliance, asset delivery integrity, and authenticity of the audited donation matters were verified without error.
Care for People and Assistance with Disaster Relief

In January 2025, the Group donated RMB 2 million in cash and relief supplies valued at nearly RMB 500,000 to the earthquake-stricken region in Shigatse, Tibet, for post-disaster resettlement and reconstruction, aiding the disaster-stricken area in overcoming over the difficulties.

The Shenzhen subsidiary of the Group contributed to the national strategy for rural revitalization through 'Consumption-based Poverty Alleviation' by purchasing gift boxes of local specialty agricultural products from Linquan County in Anhui Province, and the total procurement amount reached RMB 226,800.
Since 2016, the Hunan subsidiary of the Group has promoted the re-employment of surrounding farmers, employing an average of about 2,500 farmers per year.
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

On Children's Day, the Group donated RMB 45,000 to two rehabilitation centers for special children via the Shenzhen Nanshan District Charity Association. The donation will be used to purchase the various teaching tools and office equipment at the centers as well as teacher training, so as to improve the quality of rehabilitation education and support the cause of caring for special children.
The Group participated in the SGX Bull Charge Charity Run and donated SGD 10,000 (approximately RMB 54,600) to support vulnerable groups with concrete actions.

Since 2003, the Hunan subsidiary of the Group and local educational institutions in Li County, Hunan, have carried out long-term education donation activities. As of the end of the Reporting Period, the accumulated donations to the local education bureau and schools were about RMB 1,515,000. Specifically, during the Reporting Period, a total of RMB 30,000 was donated to the education fund, which was used as incentive and funding for outstanding teachers and students in need.

The Group donated a total of 18 used laptops and desktop computers to the Guangdong Education Foundation to support the construction of the 'Green Love Computer Classroom' project, thereby assisting in enhancing the level of educational facilities.

The Group donated 13 used computers to the Beijing Green & Shine Foundation to support the improvement of teaching conditions in schools in the central and western regions of Henan, Anhui, and Guizhou provinces, assisting teachers and students in enhancing the quality of teaching and learning.

The Group regards talent as the core driving force for development, commits to international human rights and labor standards, and strictly complies with the laws and regulations of each operating location. The Group safeguards employees' legitimate rights and interests, provides equal development opportunities, and fosters a diverse, equitable, and caring work environment, striving to achieve a winwin outcome between individual value creation and organizational strategy.

The Group has established a systematic human resources management and oversight framework. The Human Resources Center coordinates and manages human resources, and guides each subsidiary in implementing talent-related policies. At the same time, the Group receives an annual audit of internal control over human resources by external professional auditing organizations, during which all subsidiaries of the Group are covered in the form of sample surveys on human resource management, covering aspects of employee recruitment, contract signing, probation completion/internal transfer, employee attendance, implementation of leave policies, and remuneration and benefits distribution.

During the Reporting Period, the Group did not violate any applicable law or regulation that had a significant impact on the Group in terms of employment and employees' rights and interests. There were no strikes, lockouts or labor disputes that had an impact on its operations. Meanwhile, according to the results of internal and external audits, the Group was not exposed to any significant risks associated with human resource management and human rights.

The Group persists in legal and compliant employment and has established internal regulations, such as the Human Resource Policy , and continuously improves the recruitment mechanism. The Group highlights that employment relationships must be based on the principles of legality, fairness, honesty and integrity, mutual consent, and willingness, and follows the procedures for signing, amending, revoking or terminating the labor contracts with all employees, and strictly prohibits any form of discrimination, child labor, and forced labor.

The Group is aware of the importance of a talent pipeline to corporate development and has established internal management policies such as the CMS Recruitment Management Measures and Incentive Policies for Recommending Talents . The Group continues to enhance its supporting recruitment systems and advance end-to-end digitalization upgrades to ensure that recruitment is carried out efficiently and in an orderly manner.
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

The Group has established a talent review and reserve mechanism to meet the future strategic business needs for key talent. The Human Resources Center and its teams conduct a Group-wide talent needs assessment semi-annually, develop talent deployment strategies and corresponding recruitment plans in advance based on current staffing plans and talent demand feedback from each department. During the Reporting Period, the Group's Human Resources Center developed role-based competency models for several positions, conducted talent reviews in several subsidiaries, and provided talent management and development recommendations.

To enhance internal succession planning and build a stronger pipeline and strengthen talent reserves for key positions, the Group, through cooperation with professional third-party institutions, has developed a position competency model, conducted talent reviews of prospective candidates, set up a dynamically updated reserve talent pool, and facilitated the movement of pipeline candidates into key roles, to better align talent pipeline development with business growth and needs. At the same time, relying on the school-enterprise cooperation projects, the Group deepens the interaction and cooperation with higher education institutions, and builds sustainable talent pipelines for professional roles.

The Group actively engages in talent acquisition and places importance on talent planning and ecosystem building. It has established diverse channels for talent acquisition, such as campus recruitment, experienced hiring, and internal recruitment, to continuously expand its talent team.

Experienced Hiring | • In addition to traditional social recruitment channels, such as professional human resource websites and headhunting firms, the Group has established official recruitment accounts on multiple social media and platforms to post the latest recruitment information, which helps attract potential candidates more effectively and assists job seekers in obtaining recruitment information conveniently through diverse channels. • The Group has also developed mechanisms and incentive policies for recommending excellent talents, which motivate all employees and the public to actively recommend talents. • During the Reporting Period, the Group successfully recruited 722 professionals through experienced hiring channels. The Group aligns with approximately ten United Nations and other international declarations and conventions, such as the Universal Declaration of Human Rights , the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities , and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights , and has formulated and implemented the CMS Human Rights and Employee Diversity Policy applicable to all operating entities and employees, proactively promoting the protection of its employees' human rights.

The Group has a zero-tolerance stance toward child labor and forced labor, conducts background checks before recruitment, and requires the Human Resources Center to ensure the authenticity and validity of the candidates' identity are verified during the recruitment process through inquiry, verification of identity documents and obtaining signed confirmation from candidates. The Group also encourages employees to report illegal employment cases to superiors in charge for timely investigation and follow-up actions. If any violation, such as child labor or forced labor, is found, employment will be identified as invalid, the employment contract will be immediately terminated, and the salary, benefits and other remuneration prescribed by law will be paid. Meanwhile, the Group has correspondingly established an accountability mechanism, in which relevant personnel responsible will be punished according to the severity of the circumstances to prevent a recurrence of such events. During the Reporting Period, the Group employed no child labor or forced labor.

While ensuring that its employment practices are lawful and compliant, the Group proactively promotes the protection of its employees' human rights in key areas such as recruitment and employment, and requires the Human Resources Center to review the implementation of human rights protection through conducting internal communications and investigations periodically. During the Reporting Period, the Group provided training and promotion of CMS Human Rights and Employee Diversity Policy to all employees, including anti-discrimination, anti-harassment, prohibition of forced labor and child labor, respect for employees' freedom of association, diversity, and inclusion, in order to maintain a harmonious and inclusive working environment.

text: Results of performance evaluation will be sent to employees via the Group' s online platform in a timely manner. section_title: Protection of Employees' Rights and Interests / Remuneration and Benefits
