text: The Group provides employees with fair and reasonable remuneration and benefits, ensuring that employee remuneration is not lower than the national and local minimum wage standards. It is committed to paying employees' wages in full and on time, and clearly lists the lawful deductions on pay slips to ensure transparency and fairness in remuneration payments. At the same time, the Group upholds the principle of equal pay for equal work, ensuring that male and female employees receive equal remuneration and all employees get fair and reasonable remuneration for their roles.

section_title: Protection of Employees' Rights and Interests / Remuneration and Benefits
text: The Group adopts flexible remuneration policies and allows compensation discussions depending on local living costs and needs. Meanwhile, it conducts annual remuneration reviews and adjustments for all employees, as well as refinement of qualification standards and job-fit assessment presentations to maintain a fair and effective remuneration evaluation mechanism and adjustment rules of the Group. The Group also engages an external human resource consulting firm annually to conduct market compensation benchmarking and comprehensively reviews internal remuneration levels through the analysis of role-based pay competitiveness to ensure that employees receive competitive benefits and remuneration in the market.

section_title: Protection of Employees' Rights and Interests / Remuneration and Benefits

The Group strictly complies with labor-related laws and regulations and firmly prohibits any form of forced labor. The Group implements standard statutory working hours, on that basis, offers flexible work arrangements into practice to enable employees to reasonably schedule work and leisure time according to responsibilities and department demands, thereby facilitating a better work-life balance. In the context of overtime culture not being advocated, employees who need to work overtime due to work arrangements should submit overtime requests to department heads for evaluation and approval. Upon completion of overtime work, the employees will be provided with compensatory leave or overtime pay for work performed on national statutory holidays according to regulations.

In addition, the Group ensures that all employees are entitled to statutory public holidays and paid leave according to law. In mainland China, these holidays and leave include paid annual leave, marriage leave, maternity leave, paternity leave, nursing leave, funeral leave, parental leave. Overseas, the holiday and leave principle is adapted and implemented in accordance with local laws and policies. During employees' statutory leave, the Group guarantees 100% job retention,fully respecting and protecting employees' rights and interests.

The Group is committed to building a sustainable, high-quality team of talent. Taking the corporate development strategy and employee growth needs as the foundation, it has formulated a series of training management policies, such as the Internal Trainer Management Policy , to establish a comprehensive talent development system and a clear career development path, assisting employees in achieving self-surpassing and capability enhancement.

During the Reporting Period, the Group conducted the first round of competency modeling, aiming to scientifically establish role-based competency standards and identify the competency requirements for different positions. This initiative is intended to drive the update of a matching training system, providing a precise support for talent development and cultivation, and facilitating the implementation of the Group' s talent strategy.

The Group has set up a diversified talent training system driven by the policy framework and supported by the knowledge base and system platform. Tailored to the different growth stages of employee career development, the Group offers curriculum courses focused on occupational skills, professional expertise, leadership capabilities, and general competencies. Meanwhile, the Group proactively promotes the construction of a digital training management system, and has established an online learning platform, CMS Academy, for all employees and developed AI coaching tools to further improve the accessibility, convenience, and flexibility of training. The Group also improves the follow-up and monitoring on the implementation of all kinds of training programs, and timely collects and analyzes employees' feedback, so as to maintain its high training quality.

The Group adheres to the promotion mechanism that is oriented by competence and integrity, follows the talent promotion philosophy and principle of 'internal selection, step-by-step promotion, tiered training, spiral advancement, and exceptional promotion in special period' , and has established a clear promotion evaluation mechanism and the performance management system for each role. Meanwhile, the Group establishes a promotion application system, by which employees can voluntarily apply for promotion. The Group evaluates and approves the promotion of employees based on their performance evaluation and assessment results.

Promotion results will be publicized in the form of a personnel appointment and removal announcement. Any employee objecting to the certification process or results may lodge complaints to the Human Resources Center, and the latter will review and provide feedback on the appeal within 5 business days to ensure promotion channels and opportunities are fair, transparent, and effective.

The Group strictly follows a series of internal management policies, such as the Human Resource Policy , to handle employee departure procedures. The Group' s Human Resources Center is responsible for providing comprehensive assistance to departing employees to ensure that social insurance, file management, residence permit transfer, as well as other relevant formalities are properly handled to safeguard employees' rights and interests.

The Group attaches great importance to talent retention, and endeavors to enhance employees' sense of belonging and engagement by implementing a competitive compensation and benefits system, a fair performance incentive mechanism, well-grounded training and career development pathways, and a smooth communication mechanism, thereby reducing the employee turnover rate and ensuring the stability of the Group' s talent pipeline and workforce structure.
To promote healthy talent mobility and the Group's long-term sustainable growth, the Group facilitates talent retention through various retention programs, with measures as follows:

Establishing a risk management mechanism for employee turnover, holding standardized resignation interviews with all resigning employees, to better understand their reasons for leaving, collect valuable feedback information, and then formulate internal improvement measures;
Providing employees with competitive remuneration and benefits, systematic training and development plans, and a safe and reassuring working environment;
Establishing a fair, impartial and transparent talent competition mechanism and providing broad development space and reasonable incentives for employees with excellent competence and integrity;
Providing induction training and a mentor for new hires to help them better adapt to their work and integrate into the company;
Listening to employees' feedback, analyzing their needs and helping them solve problems and difficulties at work.

In terms of organizational and talent strategy planning, the Group adheres to the principles of forwardlooking planning and disciplined execution. All personnel structure optimization strictly adheres to the business strategy orientation, achieving dynamic balance through natural attrition, internal redeployment, and reskilling and upskilling. Over the past five years, the Group did not experience largescale layoffs or major mergers/acquisitions affecting a substantial portion of the workforce.

The Group is committed to establishing open and diverse communication channels for employees to promote interaction and mutual trust among employees and between employees and the Group. It has established regular online and offline communication channels, respects employees' rights to freedom of association and collective bargaining, and conducts regular surveys to systematically collect feedback. At the same time, the Group has established an independent and confidential complaint and suggestion mechanism to ensure that employees' opinions are heard promptly and handled appropriately.

The Group respects employees' rights to freedom of association and collective bargaining. Some of the main Chinese subsidiaries of the Group have established labor unions, which represent and safeguard the legal rights and interests of all employees, actively participate in the democratic management of the main subsidiaries, and promote a harmonious relationship between the main subsidiaries and their employees. The Group supports all employees in joining the labor union and participating in related activities. The labor union has the right to bargain and negotiate with the Group on behalf of employees, and to legally sign collective bargaining agreements through collective bargaining.

To promote employee communication and organizational climate construction, during the Reporting Period, the Group organized 71 organizational climate activities, with an average satisfaction rate of 97%, and also conducted an annual organizational climate survey through questionnaires to systematically evaluate the implementation effectiveness in dimensions such as internal construction, collaboration mechanisms, and employee experience. Survey results indicate that organizational climate activities can significantly enhance team cohesion, cross-regional collaboration capabilities, and employee engagement.

The Group encourages employees to communicate with the management through the internal communication platform, email, and online or face-to-face conversations in a timely and effective manner. The Group also actively communicates with employees in the form of probation confirmation interviews, exit interviews and regular questionnaire surveys. During the Reporting Period, the Group continuously solicited feedback from all employees regarding their opinions and job satisfaction through conducting interviews, surveys and establishing real-name/anonymous dialogue channels. Meanwhile, the Group has conducted an employee engagement questionnaire survey, and the result of the survey is a score of 4.67 out of 5. Based on the survey results, the Group comprehensively considers the reasonableness of feedback and the feasibility of internal practices to formulate improvement plans, in order to establish a harmonious and healthy working environment.

The Group has established a digital complaint channel for employees: 'Employee Voice' , which supports employees to lodge complaints in real name or anonymously to encourage them to speak up. The 'Employee Voice' has been embedded in the Group' s communication platform so that employees can lodge complaints promptly when they encounter conduct that may violate the Group' s policies, including but not limited to workplace bullying, abuse of authority, discrimination, harassment, or unfair treatment, and the Group can investigate and address related events in a timely manner. During the Reporting Period, the Group continued to improve and implement complaint channel management and operation measures to ensure the standardization and effectiveness of the complaint-handling process.

Complaints are classified by the Group's Human Resources Center and handed over to the relevant departments responsible for handling based on the nature of the incidents. The handling department must provide a progress update to complainants within 5 business days upon receipt of the complaints;
Complaints involving internal fraud and external bribery are handled in accordance with CMS Anti-Fraud Management System ;
Transfer personnel and acceptance personnel who have a conflict of interest with the complaint matter, which may compromise impartial handling, must recuse themselves from the handling process.
The complainant shall evaluate the handling of the complaint after receiving the feedback, and the complaint will be closed if the complainant agrees with the handling results;
If the complainant still has questions or requires further feedback, he/she can lodge a complaint again.
Handlers shall maintain the complaint records properly, and are strictly prohibited from disclosing any personal information of the complainants or relevant information of the complaints;

The Group's Human Resources Center compiles a summary report of the complaint records every quarter for filing. Such reports are submitted to the executive directors for review after the Group's internal audit.

The Group takes measures to fully protect the legal rights, interests and claims of the complainants. For confirmed violations, the Group will impose strict penalties according to regulations and formulate response measures. For malicious accusations or false statements, the Group will hold such behaviors accountable. If the violation involves suspected legal offenses, the Group will transfer the case to judicial authorities in accordance with the law.

text: The Group has formulated a series of safety management regulations, including Production Safety Management Policy , Employee Health Management Procedure, and Emergency Response Plan , etc., and has publicly released the CMS Environmental Protection, Occupational Health and Safety Management Policy covering all full-time, part-time and intern employees, to create a healthy and safe working environment for our employees.

section_title: Ensuring the Occupational Health and Safety of Employees
text: The Group has established the occupational health and safety management/supervision team, including the ESG Committee, Administrative Department, Production Department, Audit Department, and Human Resources Center. The Group actively promotes the subsidiaries to establish a safety management system and to obtain relevant certification. section_title: Ensuring the Occupational Health and Safety of Employees

section_title: Taking Actions to Protect the Environment
text: The Group deeply integrates environmental protection into its business operations by systematically managing GHG, waste, and the use of resources. It practices responsible operations and production responsibilities, driving synergistic development between its business and the ecosystem. The Group' s business with direct impacts on the environment mainly includes pharmaceutical sales and marketing business, pharmaceutical production business and agriculture and livestock business 4 . The Group' s pharmaceutical production business is relatively small in scale. During the Reporting Period, the sales of self-produced products only accounted for around 0.7% of the Group' s revenue under the assumption that all revenue was generated from pharmaceutical product sales. Due to the Group' s business distribution characteristics, the total emission of GHG and environmental pollutants was limited, and the impact on the ecological environment was insignificant.

section_title: Taking Actions to Protect the Environment
text: The Group has established an environmental management system that combines a compliance foundation with goal-oriented guidance. Based on compliance with environmental protection-related laws and regulations in the places of operation, the Group continuously monitors policy developments, has publicly issued the CMS Environmental Protection, Occupational Health and Safety (EHS) Management Policy , and has set environmental management targets with respect to GHG emissions, waste, energy consumption, and water resource usage, striving to enhance its capabilities in addressing climate change and environmental protection. The Group's manufacturing subsidiary has received the GB/T 24001-2016/ISO 14001:2015 environmental management system certification.

section_title: Taking Actions to Protect the Environment
text: To systematically control and optimize corporate environmental practices, the Group has established an environmental governance system encompassing the Board of Directors, the ESG Committee under the Board, and the ESG Working Group. The Board of Directors of the Company is the highest-level governance body for environmental management strategy and performance. The ESG Committee under the Board is responsible for overseeing the management guidelines, policies and structures of environmental protection, overall supervising and managing ESG-related risks and opportunities, and collaborating with the Audit Department and the ESG Working Group to identify and address these risks. The ESG Working Group is primarily responsible for implementation, including the formulation of specific environmental management plans, the collection, consolidation, and analysis of data on pollution emissions, energy use, and water consumption from all responsible entities. These activities support reporting to the ESG Committee and assist the Board in continuously monitoring the Group' s management of energy conservation and emission reduction, as well as the achievement of environmental targets. During the Reporting Period, the Board of Directors of the Company and the ESG Committee reviewed the Group' s environmental management strategy, the implementation of environmental management, and the progress of environmental targets.

section_title: Taking Actions to Protect the Environment
text: The Group systematically monitors the operational effectiveness and compliance level of its environmental management system through a combination of internal and external audits.

The Audit Department conducts annual internal audits of all operational entities regarding environment and energy consumption, and compiles special audit reports for review by the ESG Committee. During the Reporting Period, the Group conducted a comprehensive on-site audit regarding the environment and energy consumption, covering the pharmaceutical production business, agriculture and livestock business, office areas, and all other operational entities. The status (such as environmental governance, environmental facilities, energy use, storage and disposal of hazardous waste, and employee safety) was comprehensively reviewed and problems of each audited entity were systematically identified, assessed, and explained in detail. Based on the audit results, the Audit Department provided recommendations to the relevant responsible entities for rectification, assisted them in formulating comprehensive improvement plans, regularly tracked the progress of corrective actions, and issued the Special Audit Report on ESG Environment and Energy Consumption.

Some of the Group' s subsidiaries are also subject to unscheduled external environmental inspections and audits every year. Among them, the Group' s manufacturing subsidiary engages a third party to carry out monthly/quarterly environmental impact monitoring and to issue reports, and also undergoes the environmental inspections by local government authorities; the Group' s Agriculture and Livestock subsidiary is subject to unscheduled law enforcement inspections by the local environmental protection authority. The local agricultural product quality and safety authority and the green food office conduct annual inspections regarding agricultural product quality and production environment. During the Reporting Period, no major environmental issue was found in all inspections.

Climate change response is a core issue in the current global development process. As a pharmaceutical company with a strong sense of social responsibility, CMS has deeply incorporated climate change issues into its long-term strategic system, systematically identified climate-related risks and opportunities, assessed the impact of various risks and opportunities on our business and financial aspects, and formulated scientific countermeasures. The Group refers to IFRS S2 Climate-related Disclosures , Appendix C2 Environmental, Social and Governance Reporting Code to the HKEX Listing Rules , and other authoritative standards and regulatory requirements. The Group comprehensively carries out management practices and information disclosures in the field of climate change, focusing on four core dimensions, i.e., governance structure, strategy, risk management, and metrics and targets.
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

CMS places great importance on the physical and transitional risks brought about by climate change, as well as the sustainable development opportunities in the process of low-carbon transition. To systematically address related challenges and opportunities, the Group has established a top-down climate change governance structure to ensure that climate issues are effectively integrated into corporate strategy, risk management, and daily operations. The Board of Directors serves as the highest decision-making body for the Group' s climate change activities. It has established an ESG Committee and an ESG Working Group, which oversee all climate change-related matters within the Group. The Board of Directors and ESG Committee review and supervise climate-related issues and work progress via quarterly meetings.

Members of the Board of Directors and the ESG Committee possess knowledge of climate-related issues and understand their impact on the Company' s business and operations. To ensure that the Board of Directors and the ESG Committee stay well-informed and updated, the Company regularly provides specialized learning sessions on climate-related policies, regulations, and global trends. It also brings in external expert opinions to continuously enhance the Board members' expertise and decision-making capabilities in managing climate-related risks and opportunities. The Board of Directors has reviewed the work plans for climate information disclosure, the identification and management of climate-related risks and opportunities, and related target-setting and implementation. At the same time, the Board of Directors systematically considers climate-related risks and opportunities brought by climate change when formulating overall strategy, business planning, major transaction decisions, risk management procedures, and related policies.

The Group assessed in detail the risks and opportunities faced by its business operations under different scenarios with qualitative and quantitative approaches. Specifically, the Group conducted quantitative analysis using a global natural hazard risk database to reassess the risk levels of the assets when they are exposed to different material physical risks under different scenarios, and to quantify the percentage of asset value vulnerable to physical risks 5 .
The Group used a climate risk assessment questionnaire to assess the physical and transition risks it may face. Specific steps are as follows:

Prepare and distribute the climate risk assessment questionnaire for the executive directors of the Company and the management personnel at and above the manager level of the Group. Experts from a professional third-party consulting firm are also invited to conduct the assessment based on their understanding of the Group's business and their professional knowledge of climate risks;

Analyze and rank the exposure of the Group to physical and transition climate risks based on questionnaire results, and determine the final risk analysis result and ranking through a combination of questionnaire-based qualitative analysis and model-based quantitative analysis;
The ESG Committee reviews and approves the analysis and ranking results, and reports the assessment results to the Board of Directors at the regular meetings;

Develop corresponding climate change mitigation and response measures, as well as strategies and targets based on the assessment result, which are supervised and tracked by the Board of Directors and the ESG Committee, in terms of the relevant actions and the accomplishment of targets.

As the physical assets held and leased by the Group (including office buildings, factories, and warehouses, etc.) are exposed to the natural environment, they may be exposed to physical risks resulting from climate change. Based on the updated analysis results under various climate change scenarios, the Group has included leased assets in the climate risk analysis, and has taken into account the climate change factors and the geographical locations of its owned and leased physical assets, and has identified the physical risks it may face and the potential impacts of the risks.

text: Extreme heat can directly damage the body's thermoregulation system through factors such as temperature and humidity, leading to serious illnesses or even death, thereby reducing labor productivity and availability, or changing the efficiency of production processes, ultimately impacting the Group's business operations;

Extreme heat may intensify electricity demand, leading to regional power shortages or grid failures, which could result in production downtime, supply chain disruptions, and delivery delays.

text: Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

To enhance the Group' s business layout and strategic planning in response to changes in the future operating environment, during the Reporting Period, the Group conducted a comprehensive reassessment and optimization of potential transition risks it may face in the future with reference to the results of climate change scenario analyses and taking into full account the Group' s business status, attributes of the pharmaceutical industry, technological iteration trends, and policy orientations within the operating jurisdiction. This ensures that the risk identification and assessment system remains in sync with the current climate change process and the pace of the Group' s strategic upgrades. The transition risks faced by CMS are mainly divided into five types, including policy and legal risk, technical risk, market risk, reputational risk and supply chain risk, respectively 7 .

text: Low-carbon technology transition is emphasized for R&D and investment.
Customer concerns and needs change constantly;
The disease incidence and transmission rates change constantly;
Loweremission products and services replace the existing ones.

Companies need to proactively restructure their energy consumption and raw material selection systems and comprehensively implement clean production processes and environmentally friendly operational procedures to solidify their green competitiveness and align with the market's preference for sustainable development entities.
Companies will prioritize collaboration with suppliers adopting green and low-carbon technologies or drive a structural reshaping of the existing supply chain framework.

Climate change affects the ecological balance, and will not only accelerate the reproduction and growth life cycle of some pathogens, but also facilitate the rapid adaptation of pathogens to the environment and speed up their mutation. Companies need to continuously carry out basic scientific research on climate change and related drugs, and improve the R&D efficiency of innovative drugs.

Customers are increasingly concerned about the carbon footprint of the value chain, and require reducing carbon emissions throughout the value chain, and have included low carbon products or ESG performance as one of the evaluation points for achieving cooperation;

In some countries/regions, increased demand from healthcare providers for products and services with relatively low GHG emission footprints will lead to substitution of pharmaceutical products with higher GHG emission footprints.

Regulatory authorities, investors, customers, consumers, and other stakeholders increasingly focus on the impact of global warming and the consequent impacts of climate change. They raise expectations for corporate actions to address these challenges with more stringent requirements for public disclosure on climate risks and low-carbon products.

The Group's Scope 2 GHG emissions mainly come from the secondary energy consumed by its business, mainly the purchased electricity from the national power grid of the locations of the assets. Sudden power or water supply outages or limits, or rises in water or electricity prices, may occur due to climate change or the national dual-carbon policies.
Climate change may affect the normal growth of raw materials, which makes it difficult for companies to acquire some raw materials; raw material prices rise because of the decrease in supply.

text: Under the 'NGFS-hot house world' scenario, it is assumed that there will be no additional measures in terms of policy, regulation or technical measures other than those already in place in 2023. The policies and regulations will not gradually become more stringent, and the market demand will not change dramatically. The world, including China, still relies mainly on fossil fuels but has made insufficient investments in low-carbon emission technologies. As the Paris Agreement fails to achieve substantial results and extreme weather events will occur more frequently in the future, CMS is mainly facing physical risks, while the transition risks are relatively less prominent and are not analyzed separately.

The Group understands proactive actions to respond to climate change will have a positive impact on its sustainable development, such as improving resource utilization efficiency, participating in carbon markets, and launching innovative products. text: The GHG emissions from the Group' s operations mainly cover two categories: Scope 1 direct emissions from the combustion of fossil fuels such as natural gas, gasoline, and diesel, and Scope 2 indirect emissions from the consumption of purchased electricity. In response to the United Nations SDGs and China' s 'Dual Carbon' goal, the Group has set up reasonable short-, medium- and long-term targets on GHG emission reduction. During the Reporting Period, the Group has achieved positive progress towards all its targets for GHG emissions.

text: Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

The Group strictly complies with relevant laws and regulations on emissions management in the places of operation, and has formulated a series of internal management regulations such as the Regulations on Environmental Protection , which clearly define controls over pollutants generated at all stages of production and operations, including wastewater, exhaust gas, solid waste, and noise. It continues to conduct monitoring of pollutant indicators to ensure emissions meet national and local environmental protection standards, to promoting coordinated development between efficient operations and environmental protection.

The Group implements systematic monitoring and management of pollutant emissions, and continuously reduces the impact of its operations on the surrounding environment. In terms of production business, subsidiaries regularly engage qualified third-party monitoring institutions each year to strictly monitor their emissions of wastewater, exhaust gas and noise to ensure emission compliance. Meanwhile, by optimizing operational management, the Group continuously enhances its whole-process prevention and control and end-of-pipe treatment capabilities, striving to build a more harmonious and cleaner production environment.

The Group extends green management to the supply chain, driving partners to fulfill their environmental responsibilities through systematic screening and continuous assessment. In supplier selection, the Group prioritizes suppliers with green concepts or relevant qualifications, requiring suppliers to provide relevant documents such as environmental system certificates, emission permits, etc., and takes waste reduction (harmful emissions such as exhaust gas, wastewater and hazardous waste) plans and arrangements into the supplier screening and assessment framework. In the annual performance review, the Group took the pollution emission and waste reduction of suppliers into consideration. If any problems are identified, this will trigger the formulation and implementation of rectification measures through communication and coordination.

During the Reporting Period, the Group was not subject to any significant administrative penalties due to pollutant emissions, and its pollutant emissions did not have any adverse impact on employees, local communities, or other groups.

The Group, in accordance with the Law of the People' s Republic of China on Prevention and Control of Water Pollution and other relevant laws and regulations, formulated and implemented internal management policies such as the Standard Operation Procedures for Use, Maintenance, and Overhaul of Wastewater Treatment Facility , thereby achieving strict control over each stage of wastewater collection, treatment, reuse and discharge. The wastewater generated by the Group mainly includes domestic and production wastewater. The Group adopts reasonable wastewater treatment processes to enhance the effectiveness of wastewater reuse, achieving the rational recycling of water resources while ensuring the wastewater is discharged in compliance with the standards.
During the Reporting Period, the Group did not directly discharge pollutants into natural water bodies such as surface water, groundwater, and seawater.
The Group' s management measures for wastewater include but are not limited to:
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

Office areas | √ Collect and monitor wastewater discharge data on a quarterly basis, analyze abnormal data, and implement optimization measures; √ Domestic wastewater is treated through multi-stage septic tanks and discharged into the municipal wastewater pipe network after reaching the standard. Pharmaceutical production areas | √ The production wastewater is treated by the self-built integrated wastewater treatment station to meet regulatory standards, and then discharged into the municipal pipe network and finally flows into the municipal wastewater treatment plant. Moreover, an automatic wastewater monitoring system is installed in the wastewater treatment station to monitor and analyze the production wastewater regularly, which is linked to the provincial environmental protection monitoring platform to realize real-time and transparent management of production wastewater; √ Regularly engaging qualified third parties to conduct wastewater monitoring, with main monitoring parameters including pH, suspended solids, ammonia nitrogen, etc.; √ Recovering relatively clean wastewater for reuse, such as for floor cleaning and toilet Agriculture and livestock areas | √ Collecting manure water from agricultural farms through sedimentation ponds and making organic fertilizers from dried animal dung through dung scrapers, to achieve the purpose of recycling; √ Growing plants around animal enclosures and parks to absorb animal manure water left outdoors; √ Adopting reasonable wastewater treatment processes to ensure that treated wastewater meets the Discharge Standard of Pollutants for Livestock and Poultry Breeding before being discharged, avoiding secondary pollution to the surrounding environment.

text: The Group strictly complies with relevant laws and regulations, such as the Law of the People' s Republic of China on the Prevention and Control of Atmospheric Pollution and the Integrated Emission Standard of Air Pollutants , and has formulated and implemented management policies such as the Regulations of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Management. In response to the requirements of the national and local environmental protection authorities, it has implemented management measures such as adopting exhaust gas treatment equipment and improving the production process to control the compliant emissions of air pollutants.

The Group' s sources of air pollution are mainly from the pharmaceutical production business, and pollutants include nitrogen oxides/sulfur dioxide/particulate matter generated by boilers due to complete and incomplete combustion. To ensure compliance with emissions, the Group' s manufacturing subsidiary engages a qualified third party to conduct monthly/ quarterly inspections on the emission of nitrogen oxides, sulfur dioxide, particulate matter, and other pollutants. During the Reporting Period, the relevant test results indicated that the Group' s emissions complied with the prescribed emission limits for air pollutants.
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development
To minimize the negative impact of exhaust gas generated in production operations on the environment, the Group takes measures including but not limited to:
√ Using natural gas boilers to reduce pollutant emissions from the source;

√ Upgrading the built-in dust collector of the cutting and shredding equipment for 'pre-treatment' in the Chinese medicine extraction workshop, and adding a large cyclone baghouse dust collector to allow dust and exhaust gas to meet the standard and be discharged at a regulated height after multi-stage treatment;

√ Using 'alkaline water spray + photo-oxidation + 15m exhaust stack' deodorization systems in wastewater treatment stations, and using 'fan collection + plasma treatment + 15m exhaust stack' smell and odor treatment systems in the Chinese medicine extraction workshop, to jointly further improve exhaust gas treatment;
√ Adopting forced exhaust ventilation and activated carbon filtration for reagent cabinets;
√ Regulating boiler operations reasonably based on the production tasks of workshops, to reduce unnecessary use for less exhaust gas emissions;
√ Engaging a third-party testing institution to sample the organized exhaust gas emitted by natural gas boilers monthly/quarterly to inspect the compliance of pollutant emissions.

The Group has formulated regulations such as the Management System of Waste Product and Material, and the Regulations on Hazardous Waste, classifies, collects, and stores non-hazardous waste, collects hazardous waste in a temporary hazardous waste storage, and regularly engages qualified third parties for disposal. It also explores pathways for the recycling and reutilization of non-hazardous waste, thereby minimizing the negative impacts of waste on the environment and surrounding residents as much as possible. During the Reporting Period, the Group did not report any soil or ground water pollution incidents caused by waste/chemical leaks.

The Group has set short-term environmental targets related to hazardous and non-hazardous waste with 2020 as the base year and 2026 as the target year. At the end of the Reporting Period, the environmental targets related to hazardous and non-hazardous waste were on track.

text: Hazardous and Non-hazardous Waste-Related Metrics and Targets The Group' s hazardous waste is mainly from laboratory waste liquids, expired chemical reagents and waste medicines, etc., in the pharmaceutical production and operation processes. The Group complies with national laws and regulations and manages hazardous waste under centralized oversight, reducing the generation of waste from the source and ensuring the proper treatment of the hazardous waste. The Group' s hazardous waste control measures include but are not limited to:
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

Procurement on Demand | √ Strictly complying with management requirements for the use of related chemical reagents, and purchasing and withdrawing these reagents based on actual need to minimize waste due to expiration whenever possible. Compliance Management | √ Strengthening the routine management of the laboratory, and standardizing the operation process of inspection and testing, to minimize the generation of chemical waste residues and waste liquids; √ Recording information regarding waste generation, transportation, treatment, and disposal, among other matters on the solid waste management information platform. Classified Storage | √ Setting up a dedicated temporary hazardous waste storage room and warning signs, and storing hazardous waste in separate categories. Compliant Handling | √ Engaging a third-party professional disposal company to transfer and dispose of hazardous waste on a regular basis. Before entering into hazardous waste disposal contracts with third parties, the Group strictly reviews their qualifications, such as the business license, the permits for operation and transportation.

text: The Group' s non-hazardous waste is mainly from routine operations and production activities, primarily including household waste, water treatment sludge, and Chinese herb residue. Through measures such as classified management and waste recycling and reuse, the Group achieved comprehensive waste reduction to mitigate the negative environmental impacts of waste. The Group' s main control measures for non-hazardous waste include but are not limited to:
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development
Fulfillment Reliable and Responsible Citizen People-Oriented Practice, Growing with Employees

Office Areas | √ Advocating a lifestyle of resource conservation and on-demand purchasing, to reduce the generation of non-hazardous waste from the source; √ Encouraging employees to take food as per their needs in the canteen to reduce the generation of kitchen waste; √ Microwaves are provided in the canteen to encourage employees to bring their own lunch boxes and use less disposable tableware; √ Encouraging the classification of waste: transporting non-recyclable waste to the garbage disposal station for centralized treatment; √ Recovering recyclable garbage such as paper, metal and plastic for treatment or recycling them to achieve comprehensive waste reduction; √ Using rechargeable batteries as much as possible for battery recycling. In addition, oil separation tanks and septic tanks are established for the primary treatment of sludge Agriculture and Livestock Areas | √ Adopting various collection devices to collect animal excrement and make it into organic fertilizers via fermentation, to realize organic recycling of non-hazardous waste.

text: The Group places high priority on noise management and exercises strict control over noise generated in the production and operation process in accordance with the Law of the People' s Republic of China on Noise Pollution Prevention and Control . The Group' s noise pollution is mainly from the pharmaceutical production business. The Group has implemented control measures at the three stages of noise generation, propagation, and reception:
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

Source Control | √ Giving priority to the use of low-noise equipment, and using horizontal centrifuges in the workshops of the Group's manufacturing subsidiary to reduce noise, to enhance control from the source; √ Isolating the noise sources from the staff activity areas by optimizing the layout of the equipment to reduce the impact of noise on employees. Propagation Pathway Control | √ Installing noise barriers outside the equipment room, and adding sound insulation cotton inside to effectively control the propagation of noise. Reception Control | √ Regularly engaging third-party professional institutions to monitor noise, ensuring that the production activities have no adverse impact on employees and surrounding residents; √ Requiring susceptible employees to wear protective equipment, and regularly carrying out training sessions, requiring employees to wear protective equipment properly; √ Strengthening production management and developing production schedules for noise- related processes to avoid long working hours of employees in noisy environments.

text: During the Reporting Period, the noise monitoring results of the Group all met the requirements and the noise did not have a significant negative impact on the employees' occupational health and the local ecological environment.

The Group integrates the concepts of circular economy and resource conservation into the entire production and operation process, abiding by the relevant laws and regulations such as the Law of the People' s Republic of China on Conserving Energy , and has formulated internal energy management policies such as the Regulations on Resource Conservation Management . Through scientific planning and refined management, it enhances the standardized management of resources such as energy, water, packaging materials, and paper, contributing to the development of a low-carbon circular economy.

Organizational structure : The Group' s manufacturing subsidiary has established a leading group for energy conservation and emission reduction to systematically advance energy-saving efforts. Energy Conservation and Emission Reduction Office and Safety & Environment specialist positions are set under the leading group, and are responsible for formulating energy efficiency standards for each production area, promoting energy-saving initiatives, and performing daily inspection and supervision to ensure effective implementation of energy conservation measures.
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

text: The Group continuously optimizes energy use efficiency to realize energy saving and consumption reduction and reduce GHG emissions. The Group mainly takes the following measures to manage the use of various energy sources:
√ Scheduling production reasonably to reduce the production time in the high-temperature summer season and reduce energy consumption;

√ Setting air-conditioning and refrigeration equipment in the warehouse area to the most energy-saving mode, advocating turning off lights and closing doors when entering and leaving the warehouse, and enhancing the awareness of electricity conservation; strengthening inspections and maintenance to ensure the normal operation of electrical equipment;
√ Ensuring that work is completed in the daytime to minimize the duration of night lighting and to reduce the energy consumption of workshops;
√ Assigning dedicated personnel to conduct routine supervision and inspection of the use of electricity, and turn off electrical equipment on time.
√ Incorporating electricity-saving tips during breaks of training sessions or meetings to enhance employees' awareness of energy conservation;

√ Reducing the use time of air conditioners in summer and setting domestic air conditioners at 26° C, and regularly maintaining air conditioners; installing shading curtains to reduce direct sunlight and air-conditioning energy consumption;
√ Rearranging unreasonable and energy-wasting electrical wiring in office areas;

√ Phasing out old electrical appliances, and utilizing LED energy-saving lamps in all lighting places where possible; adopting solar energy equipment for water heaters, streetlights and surveillance facilities.
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

text: The Group strictly complies with the Water Law of the People' s Republic of China and is committed to achieving efficient and circular use of water resources in its operations, minimizing the impact of water consumption on the environment and local communities. During the Reporting Period, the Group did not experience any water-related risks.

During the Reporting Period, by referring to the Water Risk Filter, a global tool for assessing water risk developed by World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF), the Group updated the water resource risk assessment for the areas where all physical assets are located with the update of its physical asset portfolio. The assessment aims to scientifically identify and quantify the diversified risks faced by each operating location at the basin level, with a focus on basin physical risks, basin regulatory risks, and basin reputational risks.

text: To address water-related risks and reduce water consumption, all subsidiaries of the Group have developed water use monitoring and management mechanisms, and the Group' s manufacturing subsidiary conducts a routine inspection of purified water once a week and a systematic verification once a year in accordance with the methods specified in the Pharmacopoeia of the People' s Republic of China ; according to the requirements of national standards, drinking water is inspected once a month, and a qualified third-party institution is commissioned for annual audit and inspection. Hunan Agriculture and Livestock, a subsidiary of the Group, formulated the Hunan Agriculture and Livestock Water Testing Methods . Adopting the inspection methods of 'visual inspection, odor detection, observation, taste testing, and verification' , the tap water is inspected every month, and the health inspection and quarantine authorities conduct onsite centralized inspection and testing once a year, thereby ensuring that the water quality meets the standard and guaranteeing water safety.

The Group' s water consumption mainly arises from domestic water used by employees in office areas, production and cleaning processes in pharmaceutical production areas, irrigation in agricultural areas, and water use for poultry and livestock farming. The Group has adopted specific water-saving measures for different business areas, including but not limited to:
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

Office Areas | √ Upgrading taps to water-saving taps in offices, dormitories, canteens and other places; √ For green-space watering, utilizing water-saving equipment such as portable rotary sprinklers to conduct targeted and scheduled sprinkling; √ Replacing aged and leaky equipment, commissioning auto-flushing facilities in office areas, shortening auto-flushing time, and properly adjusting flushing intervals; √ Standardizing the use of water for landscaping and making appropriate use of treated water from the wastewater treatment station for irrigation; √ Strengthening environmental protection training, setting up publicity boards on environmental protection and resource conservation, clarifying water-saving standards, and enhancing employees' water-saving awareness. Pharmaceutical Production Areas | √ Closely metering and monitoring all water-using segments in each workshop to strengthen the management of production water consumption; √ Carrying out monthly inspections, overhauls, and maintenance of the water supply system, and fixing all leakage and dripping points; √ Treating cooling water from production in workshops and wastewater from domestic use and production through the wastewater treatment station to realize reasonable recycling. Agriculture and Livestock Areas | √ Upgrading the water equipment for livestock and poultry breeding to automatic water- saving equipment; √ Collecting and using natural precipitation for irrigation to reduce the use of additional water sources; √ Using drip irrigation drinking systems in chicken coops to reduce drying, evaporation, etc. due to weather and so on.

text: The Group is committed to reducing the use of packaging materials and paper, and to enhancing the recyclability and circular utilization rate of packaging materials, thereby mitigating negative impacts on the surrounding environment. The Group has formulated the Regulations on Acceptance, Storage and Distribution of Labels, Package Inserts and Packaging Materials and the Regulations on Material Requisition , setting out clear requirements for the requisition and management of packaging materials to achieve efficient resource utilization.

The packaging materials consumed by the Group mainly include cartons, glass, plastics, etc. While meeting market and production demands, the Group has also taken the following material recycling and reduction measures to proactively and effectively reduce the consumption of packaging materials:
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development
√ Stipulating that all packaging materials shall meet environmental protection requirements and clearly displaying the nationally recognized packaging recycling label;
√ Replacing the packaging materials of certain products with recyclable packaging materials;
√ Setting up packaging material recycling sites at warehouses, to classify and recover recyclable packaging boxes and materials generated from inbound and returned products,aswell as other sources;
√ Using reusable materials such as damaged and used cartons and separation films for other filling purposes;
√ Integrating the concept of environmental protection into packaging design.
√ Using machines for packaging, carrying out training for packaging positions, and conducting inspection and maintenance for packaging machines to reduce waste of packaging materials;
√ Delivering goods in whole packages whenever possible to reduce the use of packaging materials.

The Group explicitly incorporates environmental requirements into the procurement of packaging materials, gives priority to certified environmental materials under the same conditions, and requires cooperating packaging material suppliers to provide certificates of the environmental quality management system. Among them, packaging cartons for transportation are required to comply with the requirements of GB/T 6543-2025 Single-wall and double-wall corrugated boxes for transport packages.
The Group positively promotes a paperless and digitalized working environment to reduce paper consumption and facilitate green office:
√ Standardizing paper use, and promoting double-sided printing & copying and diversified use of paper;
√ Setting wastepaper recycling bins to encourage the secondary use of paper with no confidential information;
√ Comprehensively advancing digitalization, improving operational efficiency through online systems, and reducing reliance on paper-based processes;
√ Using electronic documents in place of paper documents as much as possible in administrative work and communications with relevant parties.
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

The Group deeply recognizes that the normal operation of its business is closely intertwined with a healthy and well-functioning ecosystem, and therefore proactively takes preventive measures to minimize adverse impacts on the ecological environment and biodiversity. The Group strictly abides by the Forest Law of the People' s Republic of China, the Law of the People' s Republic of China on Wildlife Protection and other relevant laws and regulations, and the United Nations' Convention on Biological Diversity and other international conventions, and has developed internal policies including the CMS Environmental Protection, Occupational Health and Safety (EHS) Management Policy , providing institutional safeguards for biodiversity conservation.

The Group pledges to maintain zero deforestation in future operations and systematically manage the potential impacts of its business activities on the ecological environment and biodiversity. The Group prioritizes the use of environmentally friendly technologies and materials and, in planning new, renovation or expansion projects, intentionally avoids locations with important biodiversity and environmentally sensitive areas, and adopts technologies and measures with a lower environmental impact to avoid negative effects. If negative impacts occurred, the Group will take remedial measures in a timely manner.

The Group also systematically integrates biodiversity protection into value chain management. In the upstream R&D stage, the Group requires Contract Research Organizations (CROs) that conduct preclinical animal studies to strictly comply with relevant laws and regulations, adhere to animal welfare and ethical principles in accordance with applicable guidelines, and follow Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) for non-clinical laboratory studies, thereby ensuring the scientific rigor and regulatory compliance of such studies. In the downstream supply chain stage, the Group actively advocates and encourages suppliers to promote biodiversity protection in their operations and business activities. Through coordinated, end-to-end value chain management, the Group is committed to fulfilling its responsibility for ecological sustainability while achieving business objectives.

During the Reporting Period, the Tibet subsidiary of the Group conducted a number of public welfare activities in support of the Nelang Ecological and Cultural Conservation Center in Lhasa, Tibet, including guidance on warehouse management and mainenance and repair of the solar power station, etc., in order to assist in the conservation of snow leopard habitat and the construction of protected areas.
The Group has taken various measures for the protection of the ecological environment and biodiversity, including but not limited to:
Environmental Protection, Green and Low-Carbon Development

Office Areas | √ Effectively managing waste generated in daily office activities and employee activities, advocating and practicing biodiversity conservation, and ensuring that different types of waste are properly sorted and disposed of and will not pollute soil, water source and habitat; √ Enhancing the ecological awareness of employees through promoting and educating biodiversity conservation and implementing multi-level practices, and encouraging participation in environmental protection practices. Pharmaceutical Production Areas | √ Regulating procurement to prevent over-exploitation, destruction of biodiversity, and other behaviors that damage the ecological environment; √ Enhancing greening and ecological restoration in plant areas to protect the surrounding water and soil resources. Agriculture and Livestock Areas | √ Promoting harmless agriculture and livestock production technology, institutionalization of the ecological environmental protection works, and the manufacturing of environment- friendly agricultural and livestock products, to control and mitigate environmental pollution; √ Conducting daily cleaning of animal enclosures and regular sanitary inspections to reduce the impact of the breeding area on the surrounding air and water; √ Setting up double-layer protection in the breeding area to strictly prevent pollution of the surrounding environment; √ Collecting and using natural precipitation for irrigation to reduce the consumption of purchased water sources.

text: ESG Aspects, General Disclosure and KPIs | Chapter Part B: Mandatory Disclosure Requirements This part sets out disclosure requirements that must be included in an issuer' s ESG report on a mandatory basis. Governance Structure | A statement from the board containing the following elements: (i) a disclosure of the board's oversight of ESG issues; (ii) the board's ESG management approach and strategy, including the process used to evaluate, prioritise and manage material ESG-related issues (including risks to the issuer's businesses); and (iii) how the board reviews progress made against ESG-related goals and targets with an explanation of how they relate to the issuer's businesses. | ESG Governance Strategy Reporting Principles | Materiality: The ESG report should disclose: (i) the process to identify and the criteria for the selection of material ESG factors; (ii) if a stakeholder engagement is conducted, a description of significant stakeholders identified, and the process and results of the issuer's stakeholder engagement. | About the Report A description of, or an explanation on, the application of the following Reporting Principles in the preparation of the ESG report: Quantitative: Information on the standards, methodologies, assumptions and/or calculation tools used, and source of conversion factors used, for the reporting of emissions/energy consumption (where applicable) should be disclosed. | About the Report Consistency: The issuer should disclose in the ESG report any changes to the methods or KPIs used, or any other relevant factors affecting a meaningful comparison. | About the Report Reporting Boundary | A narrative explaining the reporting boundaries of the ESG report and describing the process used to identify which entities or operations are included in the ESG report. If there is a change in the scope, the issuer should explain the difference and reason for the change. | About the Report Part C: 'Comply or explain' Provisions This part sets out provisions to be reported on by an issuer in the ESG report on a 'comply or explain' basis.

text: 14 The air pollutant statistics of the Group mainly covers the exhaust gas generated from its production operations. The annual emission of air pollutants is an estimated value, which is calculated from the total natural gas consumption of the boiler, the fixed gas consumption rate of the boiler, and the emission rate. The emission rate comes from the test report of a professional third party hired by the Group, so the emission rate is related to the production status and fuel quality at the test time point. During the Reporting Period, the increase in air pollutant emissions was primarily attributable to higher production volumes driven by business demand.

15 The wastewater generated by the Group primarily consists of domestic sewage and production wastewater.The year-on-year increase was mainly due to higher domestic wastewater arising from a larger headcount, as well as increased production wastewater generated to meet business demand. 16 The direct GHG emissions (Scope 1) primarily arise from fuel consumption for production activities and daily operations. The year-on-year increase was mainly attributable to higher natural gas usage driven by increased production demand.

17 The indirect GHG emissions (Scope 2) mainly arise from indirect emissions due to the consumption of externally purchased electricity during the Group's operations and production processes. In 2025, 2024 and 2023, GHG emissions in Hong Kong were calculated with reference to the emission factors disclosed in HK Electric's Sustainability Report for 2024, 2023 and 2022, respectively. For Macau, the emission factors applied in 2023 and 2024 were the operating-region emission factors; in 2025, GHG emissions in Macau were calculated with reference to the emission factors disclosed in Companhia de Electricidade de Macau (CEM)'s 2024 Sustainability Report. For operating locations outside Hong Kong and Macau, the relevant emission factors of the countries/regions were used. In particular, for 2025, the electricity emission factor for Mainland China adopted the grid emission factor of 0.5306 tCO2/MWh as specified in the Announcement on the release of the 2023 Electricity Carbon Dioxide Emission Factors, issued by the the Ministry of Ecology and Environment on 31 December 2025.

18 During the Reporting Period, the indirect GHG emissions (Scope 3) changed compared to last year, mainly due to two factors: 1) in 2025, Scope 3 emissions under 'Upstream Transportation and Distribution' decreased mainly due to optimization of transportation modes and routes; this category captures only emissions from orders for which the Group is responsible for arranging transportation under the agreed trade terms with upstream suppliers (rather than all orders); This category specifically accounts for emissions arising from orders where transportation is arranged by the Group according to predefined trade agreements with upstream manufacturers, rather than encompassing all orders placed by the Group; 2) the sample of the employee commuting questionnaire changes in the composition (e.g., an increase in the number of employees who commute long distances and by private vehicles) and an increase in the number of employees have led to an increase in GHG emissions(Scope 3) in the category of 'Employee Commuting'. Please refer to Appendix V for the detailed calculation method of GHG emissions(Scope 3).

text: 19 During the Reporting Period, the hazardous waste was mainly generated from laboratory analytical tests and disposal of discarded pharmaceuticals in the pharmaceutical production business. The increase of the hazardous waste compared to the same period last year was mainly due to the increase in the generation of discarded pharmaceuticals as a result of business demand changing.

20 During the Reporting Period, the non-hazardous waste was mainly generated from household garbage, sludge from water treatment processes and Chinese herb residue in the pharmaceutical production business. The increase compared to the same period last year was mainly due to changes in business demand, which led to higher generation of Chinese herb residue.

21 During the Reporting Period, Natural gas was primarily consumed as fuel for the Group's pharmaceutical production business. Year-on-year consumption increased mainly due to changes in business demand, which drove higher fuel usage.

22 During the Reporting Period, diesel consumption primarily related to transportation vehicles used in the pharmaceutical production business. Year-on-year diesel usage decreased mainly due to adjustments to transportation modes.
